oddchem-distillai.zh: 圆底蒸馏瓶接着蛇形冷凝管，正把一颗发光的小型人工智能脑蒸馏成一串晶莹液滴落入接收瓶，脑中迸出细小电路火花。淡蓝绿玻璃配暖色高光——它想从脑子里提取思路，结果只提出了蒸馏要求。
oddchem-distillai.en: A round-bottom flask joined to a coiled condenser, distilling a glowing miniature AI brain into shimmering droplets that fall into a receiving flask, tiny circuit sparks crackling from the brain. Pale blue-green glass with warm highlights: it wanted to extract ideas and produced only a distillation request.

oddchem-serpent.zh: 一支盘成蜿蜒蛇形的玻璃冷凝管，蛇首在顶端，发光液体沿螺旋管流动。淡蓝玻璃配暖色高光，19 世纪科学插画风——冷凝的活儿它干得比原装好，只是没人敢在夜里看着它工作。
oddchem-serpent.en: A coiled serpentine condenser shaped like a slithering glass snake, a small serpent head at the top, glowing liquid flowing through the spiral. Pale blue glass with warm highlights, in the style of 19th-century scientific illustration: it condenses better than the original, though nobody watches it work at night.

oddchem-eyeball.zh: 形如巨大人眼的玻璃滴定管，刻度环刻在虹彩四周，底部旋塞滴出发光液滴，虹膜旋着细小星座。淡蓝玻璃配暖色高光——它用一只眼睛盯着刻度，顺便把星星也读了。
oddchem-eyeball.en: A glass burette shaped like a giant human eyeball, a graduated scale etched around the iris, a stopcock at the bottom releasing glowing droplets, tiny constellations swirling in the iris. Pale blue glass with warm highlights: it reads the graduations with one eye, and reads the stars on the side.

oddchem-nested.zh: 三只锥形烧瓶层层嵌套如回响幻象，最内层悬浮一颗发光小球，玻璃壁间缭绕淡淡雾气。淡蓝绿玻璃配暖色高光——同一份溶液被倒了三次，第一次像实验，后两次像回声。
oddchem-nested.en: A triple-nested Erlenmeyer flask, three conical flasks inside one another like echoing illusions, a tiny glowing sphere suspended at the centre, faint mist between the glass walls. Pale blue-green glass with warm highlights: the same solution poured three times — the first an experiment, the rest an echo.

oddchem-gears.zh: 一支分液漏斗环抱黄铜齿轮，齿轮绕玻璃身缓缓转动，两不相溶的发光液体在瓶内分成两层，底部一只齿轮旋塞。淡蓝玻璃配暖黄铜高光——它一边分层一边自己拧开自己，省了半道工序。
oddchem-gears.en: A separatory funnel ringed with brass toothed gears rotating around its glass body, two immiscible glowing liquids separating into layers, a tiny gear stopcock at the bottom. Pale blue glass with warm brass highlights: it separates while unscrewing itself, saving half the procedure.

oddchem-stars.zh: 一支高量筒内盛着一颗发光夜空，浮星与一弯小月悬于液间，玻璃上刻着刻度，顶端软木塞。淡蓝玻璃配暖色高光——量筒量的是夜空，那道刻度至今没人敢往下读。
oddchem-stars.en: A tall graduated cylinder holding a small glowing night sky, floating stars and a crescent moon suspended in the liquid, measurement markings etched up the glass, a cork stopper on top. Pale blue glass with warm highlights: the cylinder measures the night sky, and nobody has dared read below the first mark.

trades-cooper.zh: 箍桶匠抱着一只刚上完箍的橡木桶，木槌还攥在手里。他抬眼看桶沿的那一下，是他一天里唯一表示满意的动作——手艺人不太会说话，桶替他说了。
trades-cooper.en: The cooper cradles a freshly hooped oak barrel, mallet still in hand. The glance he gives the rim is the only sign of satisfaction he offers all day — craftspeople talk poorly, and the barrel says it for them.

trades-clockmaker.zh: 老修表匠把一枚开盖黄铜怀表举到眼前，镊子尖几乎没进机芯。整站都催快，只有他愿意为半秒停下来。表走得快慢是别人的事，他只管它准。
trades-clockmaker.en: The old clockmaker holds an open brass pocket watch to his eye, tweezers almost inside the movement. The whole gallery is in a hurry; he alone will stop for half a second. Whether a watch runs fast is other people's business — he only makes it correct.

trades-leatherworker.zh: 皮匠把刚缝好的马鞍高高举起，皮围裙上的针脚密得像账本。他脸上那道疤不解释来历，围裙上的线也不必数——他做的是马鞍，不是简历。
trades-leatherworker.en: The leatherworker raises a freshly stitched saddle high, the stitches on his apron dense as an account book. The scar on his face explains nothing, and the seams need no counting: he makes saddles, not résumés.

trades-cottoncarder.zh: 弹棉匠拉着大弓弦，一团雪白棉絮顺着弦炸开，笑得像个抢到糖的孩子。这活计在今天已经没人接，他还在做——他说棉花要弹到能听见风为止。
trades-cottoncarder.en: The cotton carder draws the great bow and a white cloud of fiber bursts along the string, grinning like a child who got the last sweet. Nobody takes the work any more, yet he still does: cotton, he says, must be beaten until you can hear wind in it.

trades-grinder.zh: 磨刀匠把宽刃菜刀按在湿磨石上，水珠溅到袖口。他磨的刀进不了档案，进得了灶台——在他看来这反而是更难看的评价：一把刀好不好，最后要由吃饭的人说。
trades-grinder.en: The knife grinder presses a broad cleaver onto a wet whetstone, droplets reaching his sleeve. His blades will never enter an archive, only a kitchen — which he rates the harder brief: how good a knife is gets decided by whoever eats with it.

trades-papercraft.zh: 纸扎匠托着一匹红绿描金的纸马，笔还捏在另一只手里。他做的马不会跑，但烧起来能跑很远——这在他看来不是缺陷，是一种更划算的运输方式。
trades-papercraft.en: The paper artisan holds up a red-and-green painted paper horse, brush still in his other hand. His horses never run, but burned they travel a long way — not a defect, in his view, but a cheaper form of transport.

trades-dyer.zh: 染匠挑起一段滴水的靛蓝布，脚下陶缸冒着酸气的白汽。他的手臂和衣襟被染渣染透了，迟早有一天会分不清哪块是布、哪块是人。
trades-dyer.en: The dyer lifts a dripping length of indigo cloth; white steam rises from the ceramic vat at his feet. Dye has soaked his arms and his robe alike, and sooner or later he will not be able to tell cloth from skin.

trades-basketweaver.zh: 编竹匠提起刚编好的圆竹篮，篾条编得密实发亮。他脚边那些卷曲的竹屑说明一件事实：他不是把竹子变成篮子，他是把竹子剩下的部分也一并安排妥当。
trades-basketweaver.en: The basket weaver lifts a freshly woven round basket, the strips tight and glossy. The curled shavings at his feet give away the real skill: he does not just turn bamboo into a basket, he also finds a use for what is left over.

opera-spear.zh: 武生把一杆红缨长枪横在身前，双翎随亮相一颤。他脸上的红是为气势上的，靠甲上的龙是给自己壮胆的——枪是真的沉，翎是真的痒。
opera-spear.en: The wusheng levels his red-tasseled spear, twin plumes quivering as he strikes his pose. The red on his face is for presence, the dragon on his armour for courage — the spear is genuinely heavy and the plumes genuinely itchy.

opera-fan.zh: 花旦把绢面团扇举到腮边，露出半双含笑的眼睛。珠翠头面一件不少，扇子却挑最素的那柄——按她的说法，遮掩是手艺，露多少才是功夫。
opera-fan.en: The huadan raises her silk fan to her cheek, revealing half of a smiling pair of eyes. The beaded headdress is complete, yet she chose the plainest fan — in her line of work, concealment is craft; how much to show is the kung fu.

opera-jing.zh: 净角一声喝令停在半空，脸谱纹样怒目圆睁，长髯飘起三寸。雉鸡翎在盔头上颤，其实是全场最贵的部分——他演的是气势，翎演的是高度。
opera-jing.en: The jing's command hangs mid-air: painted patterns wide-eyed, the long beard lifting three inches. The pheasant plumes tremble on his helm — the costliest part of the whole look. He plays the fury; the plumes play the altitude.

opera-laosheng.zh: 老生拈着长髯沉吟，深蓝袍子和黑方巾收拾得一丝不乱。整出戏都在赶时间，只有他这个动作被允许慢放——捋须三下，代表想了半辈子。
opera-laosheng.en: The laosheng strokes his long beard in thought, his deep-blue robe and black square hat in faultless order. The whole opera is rushing; only this gesture is allowed to run slow. Three strokes of the beard, and half a lifetime of deliberation.

opera-chou.zh: 丑角歪着小帽挤出鼻梁上一道白粉，短打青橙撞色，一蹦三跳。他是台上的漏洞，专负责把绷紧的戏戳个口子——白鼻梁一出现，观众就知道可以喘气了。
opera-chou.en: The chou tilts his little hat around a white nose patch, turquoise-and-orange acrobat colours, three skips per leap. He is the flaw in the show, the one who punctures its tension — when the white patch appears, the audience knows it may breathe again.

opera-qingyi.zh: 青衣甩开两条白水袖，人立在袖影中央，神色端庄里压着一点哀愁。淡紫长裙不沾水，水袖替她哭——按青衣的规矩，眼泪不能自己出门，得让袖子代劳。
opera-qingyi.en: The qingyi flings out her two white water sleeves, standing at the centre of their shadow, dignity holding down a thread of sorrow. The lavender gown stays dry; the sleeves weep for her — a qingyi's tears never leave on their own; the sleeves carry them out.

seamonsters-serpent.zh: 碧浪海龙从翻涌的浪花里昂起青绿长身，S 形蜿蜒，龙首带须还咧着嘴笑。它本是被冲上岸的一截旧缆绳，泡够海水后自己长出了鳞。传说谁在风暴里看见它船就不会翻——但目前只验证过透明背景上的那一条。
seamonsters-serpent.en: The tidal sea serpent rears its teal scaled body from churning waves, curving in an S, whiskered snout grinning. It began as a length of old hawser washed ashore, growing scales after enough soak in seawater. Legend says whoever sees it in a storm keeps their ship — though only the transparent-background one has been verified.

seamonsters-kraken.zh: 紫潮克拉肯八条触手张牙舞爪，圆头咧嘴露着黄牙，大眼滴溜溜转。它住在本站最深的缓存里，平时盘成一团睡午觉，一被点开就精神抖擞。它从没缠过船，只是把透明背景当成了自己的墨水瓶。
seamonsters-kraken.en: The violet kraken flings eight writhing tentacles, bulbous purple head grinning yellow fangs, big eyes darting. It lives in the site's deepest cache, coiled asleep by day, alert the moment it is opened. It has never seized a ship — it only mistook the transparent background for its own inkpot.

seamonsters-crab.zh: 赤甲巨蟹双钳高举，红壳上缀满藤壶，眼柄顶着凸出的大眼。它原本是码头边一只普通青蟹，被画师多添了两道红漆后升级成怪兽。它不横着走了，改为正面威风——至少在自己的透明背景里。
seamonsters-crab.en: The crimson shell crab raises both pincers, red armour speckled with barnacles, bulging eyes on stalks. It was an ordinary green crab by the dock until a painter added two coats of red and promoted it to monster. It no longer scuttles sideways — it faces forward, at least within its own transparent background.

seamonsters-jelly.zh: 幽灵水母的半透明伞盖泛着粉紫柔光，触须随风飘荡，伞下还挂着一张温柔笑脸。它不螫人，只负责在透明背景里安静发光，把经过的看图人照得心里一软。它从没漂走过，因为没地方比 PNG 更稳当。
seamonsters-jelly.en: The ghost jellyfish's translucent bell glows pink and violet, wispy tentacles drifting, a gentle smiling face inside. It never stings — it only glows quietly on the transparent background, softening the heart of whoever looks. It has never drifted away; no place is steadier than a PNG.

seamonsters-walrus.zh: 长牙海象魔圆滚滚扑来，两根螺旋长牙白得发亮，鳍肢张开憨态可掬，皮上还点着藤壶。它被画成怪兽纯属误会——本来只是只爱打哈欠的海象，画师嫌它太乖，硬塞了两根獠牙凑数。它在透明背景里扑空过无数次。
seamonsters-walrus.en: The tusked walrus-fiend lunges on its blubbery body, two spiralled ivory tusks gleaming, flippers splayed, barnacle freckles on its hide. It became a monster by mistake — an ordinary yawning walrus the painter found too tame, bolting on two tusks for show. It has lunged into empty space countless times on the transparent background.

seamonsters-angler.zh: 深渊灯笼鱼咧着满口尖牙，深蓝圆身，头顶挂着一盏发光小灯笼，一只大眼乌溜溜亮。那盏灯本是它钓晚饭的家伙，现在改行给看图人指路。它从没钓到过鱼，倒是照亮了不少透明背景。
seamonsters-angler.en: The abyss anglerfish grins with sharp fangs, round deep-blue body, a glowing lantern dangling above, one big luminous eye. That lantern once lured its dinner; now it guides viewers instead. It has never caught a fish, but it has lit up plenty of transparent backgrounds.

plantfolk-tophat.zh: 礼帽蘑菇先生歪戴黑高顶礼帽，单片眼镜架在眼上，酒红领结系在脖间，菌柄挺着圆肚，小树枝手臂叉腰。他从不长孢子，只长派头。据传他每天在透明背景里给自己掸三次礼帽灰。
plantfolk-tophat.en: The top-hat mushroom gentleman tilts a black topper, brass monocle over one eye, burgundy bow tie at the throat, cream stem belly proudly out, twiggy arms akimbo. He never grows spores, only posture. Rumor says he dusts his hat three times a day against the transparent background.

plantfolk-scarf.zh: 围巾仙人掌圆身子裹着粗针织红条纹围巾，红手套小胳膊缩在身侧，头顶开朵小粉花，一脸惬意。它不扎人，因为刺都藏进了毛线里。它在透明背景里过的冬天，比谁都暖。
plantfolk-scarf.en: The wool-scarf cactus wraps its round body in a chunky striped scarf, stubby mittened arms tucked in, a little pink flower on top, perfectly content. It never pricks — every spine is hidden in the wool. Its winter on the transparent background is warmer than anyone's.

plantfolk-lotus.zh: 和服荷花层层粉白花瓣拢成衣襟，系着花纹腰带，眉眼低垂浅浅含笑，叶手轻摇小折扇，根部收拢如裙裾。她不结莲蓬，只结仪态。据传每开一次扇子，透明背景就安静一分。
plantfolk-lotus.en: The kimono lotus folds layered pink-and-white petals into robes, a patterned obi at the waist, eyes lowered in a gentle smile, a leaf-hand tilting a tiny fan, roots gathered like a hem. She bears no seed pod, only grace. They say each unfurl of her fan quiets the transparent background a little more.

plantfolk-sunflower.zh: 背带裤向日葵金黄花瓣戴成王冠，一条背带滑下肩，脸颊沾泥点，一手拎小铁皮壶一手挥手欢呼。它是本站最吵的园丁，也是唯一会浇自己的花。它在透明背景里从不缺水，因为壶里永远满着。
plantfolk-sunflower.en: The overalls sunflower wears golden petals like a crown, one denim strap slipped off the shoulder, dirt-smudged cheeks, a tiny watering can in one leaf-hand and the other waving. The site's loudest gardener and the only one who waters itself. On the transparent background it never runs dry — the can stays full.

plantfolk-ivy.zh: 兜帽藤蔓披一袭深绿连帽斗篷，帽檐下只露两只狡黠发亮的眼睛，心形小叶顺衣摆垂落，卷须细臂悄声掀着兜帽。它不爬墙，只爬透明背景。据传它偷过不止一顶别人的帽子，但没人能证明。
plantfolk-ivy.en: The hooded ivy drapes a deep-green cloak, only two sly glowing eyes from the hood shadow, heart-shaped leaves along the hem, a tendril raising the hood. It climbs no wall, only the transparent background. Rumor credits it with more than one stolen hat, though no proof exists.

plantfolk-tulip.zh: 雨靴郁金香在红瓣花冠里绽着笑脸，踩明黄雨靴跨步溅水，卷曲花茎当手臂撑着波点小伞，身边飘着雨珠。它不躲雨，反而专挑水坑走。它在透明背景里从没淋湿过，因为雨从不真的落下。
plantfolk-tulip.en: The rainboot tulip grins from its red-and-cream bloom, striding in bright yellow wellies, curly stem arms holding a polka-dot parasol, raindrops drifting near. It avoids no puddle — it seeks them out. On the transparent background it has never been wet, for the rain never truly falls.

metalfolk-gnome.zh: 黄铜小矮人戴着尖顶铜帽，卷曲白胡子垂到胸前，红鼻子圆得发亮，小手提一盏黄铜小灯。铜面划痕细密，暖色包浆里缀着几点铜绿。它是这一批里唯一还带灯的，说灯是给自己照路的——好让抽屉里的其他金属人看见它没在偷懒。
metalfolk-gnome.en: The brass gnome wears a pointed cap, a curly white beard down to his chest and a round red nose, small hands carrying a little brass lantern. Fine scratches cover the metal, warm patina broken by flecks of verdigris. He is the only one of the batch who still brings a light — to show the other metal folk in the drawer that he is not slacking off.

metalfolk-clockwork.zh: 发条机械少年圆铜头顶着一枚上弦钥匙，胸口小窗里齿轮咬合清清楚楚，一只圆玻璃眼嵌在磨旧的铜皮外套上，短手短腿抬起招手。他每天上三次弦，走三步歇一步。本站不修他，只保证他每次停下来的地方，都刚好在透明背景的正中间。
metalfolk-clockwork.en: The clockwork boy wears a wind-up key on his rounded brass head, gears meshing visibly behind a small chest window, one round glass eye set in a worn copper coat, stubby limbs raised in greeting. He winds himself three times a day, walks three steps, then rests. Nobody here repairs him — only guarantees that wherever he stops, it is dead centre of the transparent background.

metalfolk-knight.zh: 青铜小骑士顶着带小缨的圆盔，圆盔正面开着个圆孔，一手举短剑，一手挎圆盾，短腿立正站得笔直。铜绿从甲缝里渗出来，划痕顺着披风纹路走。它个子小到只配给糖罐看家，但站姿从不含糊——立正就是立正，不许晃。
metalfolk-knight.en: The bronze knight wears a plumed round helm with a hole punched in the front, short sword raised in one hand, round shield on the other, stubby legs standing at attention. Verdigris seeps from the seams, scratches following the lines of his cape. He is too small to guard anything but a sugar jar, yet his posture is never in doubt: attention means attention, and no wobbling.

metalfolk-drummer.zh: 锡皮小鼓手戴着圆筒军帽咧嘴笑，双臂扬起鼓槌敲肚前那面小军鼓，一腿跨出行进步伐。红蓝油漆剥落成一片片，露出底下发乌的锡皮。它敲的曲子只有三拍，前两拍热闹，第三拍留给安静——本站不允许噪声超过两拍。
metalfolk-drummer.en: The tin drummer grins beneath a shako cap, both arms up with drumsticks over the little drum on his belly, one leg marching forward. Red and blue paint flakes away to dull tin beneath. His tune runs to three beats: two loud ones and one left for silence — this gallery does not allow noise beyond the second beat.

metalfolk-scribe.zh: 铜锈小书吏戴圆顶小帽、架一副圆眼镜，俯身凑近摊开的小书，一手捏着长鹅毛笔正要落笔。铜身通体发绿，深色锈纹与细划痕交错，只留几处暖铜色。它写得极慢，因为每落一笔都要先在透明背景上把墨迹晾干。
metalfolk-scribe.en: The verdigris scribe wears a small domed cap and round spectacles, bending over a tiny open book, a long quill poised to write. His copper body has gone green, dark patina crossing fine scratches, with only a few warm brass notes left. He writes very slowly — every stroke must first be dried against the transparent background.

metalfolk-gardener.zh: 镀金小园丁戴着草帽，系一条缀着铜绿的深铜围裙，一手拎黄铜洒水壶低头浇水，壶嘴滴出一串水珠。金箔剥落处露出底下深铜，磨旧的金边发暗。它浇的花在透明背景上，所以水珠落下去就再也不见了。
metalfolk-gardener.en: The gilded gardener wears a straw hat and a dark bronze apron spotted with verdigris, one hand tipping a brass watering can as he bends to pour, droplets falling from the spout. Chipped gold leaf reveals the bronze beneath, worn gilt edges gone dull. The flowers he waters live on a transparent background, so the water falls and is never seen again.

gizmos-bellclock.zh: 自鸣铜座钟只有巴掌大，圆脸钟盘上两根细长指针从不指向任何真实时间。小门里的钟摆自己晃着，顶上一对铜铃跟着摆一下响一声。铜壳发乌，细划痕一道叠一道，铜绿长在缝里。它每天只肯响三次，多一次都不干——规矩是它定的。
gizmos-bellclock.en: The chiming brass clock is only palm-sized, its round dial carrying two slim hands that never point at any real time. The pendulum swings on its own behind a little door, and a pair of brass bells on top rings once per swing. The shell is tarnished, scratches layered over scratches, verdigris creeping into the seams. It consents to chime three times a day and not one chime more — the rule is its own.

gizmos-grabber.zh: 多节铜机械手由一段段铜环关节连成，从底座一路弯上来，末端那对小夹爪微微张着，像随时要抓住什么。铜面被摩挲得发亮，关节缝里却积着细灰。它够不着任何东西——爪张开又合上，合上又张开，永远差着最后一寸。
gizmos-grabber.en: The jointed brass grabber is a chain of linked brass-ring segments curving up from its base, ending in a pair of small pincers held slightly open, as if about to take hold. The brass is polished bright by handling, yet grey dust has settled in the joint seams. It cannot reach anything — the pincers open and close, close and open, always a final inch short.

gizmos-steamfan.zh: 喷汽小风轮是一截黄铜立管顶着一只三叶小风轮，侧边小阀门一开，几缕白汽便推着叶片缓缓转起来。铜管发乌，细划痕绕着管身一圈圈。转得慢，但从不停；阀门一关，它就顺势把最后半圈转完，才真正安静。
gizmos-steamfan.en: The steam-puff whirligig is a short brass tube topped with a three-blade fan. Open the little valve at the side and a few wisps of white steam push the blades around, slowly. The tube is tarnished, scratches circling its length. It turns slowly but never stops; close the valve and it finishes the last half-turn before it truly settles.

gizmos-inker.zh: 自动研墨磨是一只铜制小磨盘，上截齿轮咬着一块石磨缓缓转，墨从底口一滴滴落进旁边的小铜盂。铜壳磨亮，几点铜绿藏在接缝里。它磨出来的墨永远浓得刚好——不多一滴，也不少一滴，连滴进盂里的声音都是同一个调。
gizmos-inker.en: The self-grinding ink mill is a small brass millstone turned slowly by a gear above it, ink dripping drop by drop from the bottom spout into a tiny brass cup alongside. The shell is polished bright, with a few verdigris spots hidden in the seams. The ink it grinds is always exactly right — not a drop more, not a drop less, and every drop that falls makes the same single note.

gizmos-astrolabe.zh: 折叠观星仪是几层黄铜圆盘叠在一起，每层都刻着细密星点，边缘能折出几根指针，像一张缩到巴掌大的星图。铜面发乌，划痕沿着盘的圆周走。它指着的那颗星，恰好就是它自己的位置。
gizmos-astrolabe.en: The folding astrolabe is several brass discs stacked on one another, each engraved with fine star points, with pointers folding out at the rim like a star chart shrunk to the palm of a hand. The brass is tarnished and the scratches run with the circumference. The star it indicates turns out to be exactly its own position.

gizmos-musictoy.zh: 发条八音匣是方方正正的一只小铜匣，盖上半透明小窗，窗里一个黄铜机械小人随着发条一圈圈转。侧面露着上弦旋钮，铜壳磨亮，铜绿点缀在角上。它只认那根发条——上紧它就唱，唱完就哑，绝不换调。
gizmos-musictoy.en: The clockwork music box is a small square brass case with a translucent window in the lid, and behind it a tiny brass automaton turns as the spring unwinds. The winding knob shows at one side, the shell polished bright with verdigris at the corners. It knows only that one spring — wind it and it plays, and when the song ends it falls silent rather than changing key.

leaf-starvein.zh: 星脉叶是一枚深靛蓝的泪滴形叶片，细金线在叶面上把一颗颗四角星连成整幅星座图，三颗星点最亮，还有一弯月牙挨在叶尖。象牙白叶脉从短柄向四周散开。它从来不落在地上——它属于天空，只是借了叶子的形状落在纸上。
leaf-starvein.en: The star-vein leaf is a deep indigo teardrop whose surface holds a whole constellation map, thin gold lines joining tiny four-pointed stars, three of them burning brightest, with a crescent crowding the tip. Ivory veins fan out from the short stem. It never falls to the ground — it belongs to the sky and only borrows the shape of a leaf to land on paper.

leaf-crystalhoney.zh: 晶格叶整片由六边形晶体小格拼成蜂巢，每一格都是带一点高光的棱面宝石。一条粗黄铜主脉从叶柄直贯叶尖，分出细枝脉。翠绿与墨绿的叶肉里点着薄荷绿、珊瑚粉和暖金。它不是叶子长成了宝石，是宝石决定要像一片叶子。
leaf-crystalhoney.en: The crystal-honeycomb leaf is built entirely from interlocking hexagonal cells, each one a faceted jewel carrying a small highlight. A thick polished brass midrib runs from stem to tip and branches into fine veins. Emerald and deep green flesh is dotted with mint, coral pink and warm gold. It is not a leaf that turned to gem — it is a gem that decided to look like a leaf.

leaf-gearclock.zh: 齿轮叶是长卵形，叶缘整整一圈切成圆润的黄铜齿牙，叶内三枚咬合的小齿轮和一卷金色发条充当叶脉。正中一枚象牙圆盘完全空白，没有刻度也没有数字。规矩很怪：这枚叶子只负责咬合，不负责报时——它从来不说几点。
leaf-gearclock.en: The clockwork leaf is long and oval, its edge cut into neat rounded brass teeth all the way around, with three interlocking gears and a coil of golden spring forming its veins. At the centre sits a completely blank ivory disc, no scale and no numerals. Its rule is strange: this leaf exists only to mesh, never to tell the time — it never says what hour it is.

leaf-moonphase.zh: 月相叶是完整的心形轮廓，主脉上从叶柄到叶尖排着五枚小圆月相章，先是满月，再是几弯素净的象牙月牙，章与章之间散着三颗四角小星。深梅紫叶肉配暖金边。它每一片都记着同一件事，只是记到哪一弯为止，各不相同。
leaf-moonphase.en: The moonphase leaf has a smooth, unbroken heart-shaped outline, five small round moon-phase medallions running along the midrib from stem to tip — a full moon first, then a few plain ivory crescents — with three tiny four-pointed stars scattered between them. Deep plum flesh edged in warm gold. Every leaf records the same single matter; only how far it got differs.

leaf-lampvein.zh: 灯脉叶是披针形的，叶脉其实是一根根会发光的玻璃灯管：粗琥珀主脉上分出六盏小灯泡，每盏里都亮着一小簇暖火，叶尖飘起三缕淡光。墨绿叶肉配琥珀与奶油黄，接头处是黄铜。它不靠太阳活，它自己就是那点光。
leaf-lampvein.en: The lantern-vein leaf is lance-shaped, and its veins are really glowing glass lamp tubes: a thick amber main tube with six little bulb-shaped lamps branching off, each holding a small warm flame, three pale curls of light drifting from the tip. Forest-green flesh in amber and butter yellow, brass fittings at the joints. It does not live on sunlight — it is the light itself.

leaf-doublespiral.zh: 双螺叶圆润，被裂成左右对称的两半，像双螺旋一样彼此缠绕卷曲，中间留一道象牙白细缝。午夜蓝叶肉里藏着星点和碎星，两半分别染着薄荷绿、珊瑚粉与暖金，三点珍珠光沿卷边浮动。它的一半总想去贴另一半，可中间那道缝它自己也不肯合。
leaf-doublespiral.en: The twin-spiral leaf is rounded and split into two symmetrical halves that curl around each other like a double spiral, leaving a thin ivory seam between them. Midnight-blue flesh hides stars and stardust; the halves are painted pale mint, coral pink and warm brass gold, with three pearl glints floating along the curled edges. Each half always wants to reach the other, yet the seam it refuses to close is its own.

leaf-metalscales.zh: 鳞甲叶是卵形的，整片叶面覆满层层叠叠的抛光金属鳞片，排成整齐的鳞列，每一片小鳞都沿边缘带一道亮高光。中脉是粗黄铜，鳞列之间分出细枝脉。酒红叶肉从缝里透出来，像龙鳞缝里的旧伤。它每一片鳞都朝着同一个方向护着叶心。
leaf-metalscales.en: The metal-scale leaf is oval, its whole surface covered in overlapping polished metal scales laid out in neat rows, every small scale carrying a bright highlight along its rim. The midrib is thick brass, with fine branch veins running between the rows. Wine-red flesh shows through the seams like an old wound under dragon scale. Every scale faces the same way, guarding the leaf's heart.

leaf-dewlens.zh: 露镜叶是菱形的，边缘带浅浅波浪，叶面上嵌着七颗浑圆露珠，像七枚小透镜，每颗里都收着一小卷象牙云或一颗四角星。露珠外围泛着淡涟漪。松针绿叶肉配淡天蓝。它收集的不是水，是每一个被它照见的小世界。
leaf-dewlens.en: The dew-lens leaf is diamond-shaped with gently scalloped edges, seven clear round dewdrops embedded across the blade like tiny lenses, each holding a miniature curled ivory cloud or a single four-pointed star, faint concentric ripples around them. Pine-green flesh with pale sky blue. It gathers no water — it gathers every small world it happens to see.

food-friedrice.zh: 金黄蛋炒饭盛在白瓷蓝边碗里，粒粒分明，缀着青豆、玉米和胡萝卜丁。热气照升，脚下照投影。它是全站最会撒谎的一碗饭——看着刚出锅，其实连锅都没有。透明背景上，米饭凉得比谁都快。
food-friedrice.en: Golden egg fried rice in a white bowl with a blue rim, every grain distinct, scattered with green peas, corn and carrot cubes. Steam rises on cue, shadow falls beneath. It is the biggest liar in the gallery — it looks just-fried, though no wok was ever involved. On a transparent background, fried rice cools faster than anything else.

food-sushi.zh: 寿司拼盘摆在黑木方盘上，三文鱼握寿司、金枪鱼卷和玉子烧各占一角，旁点着青芥与姜片。摆盘讲究得像要拍广告，可它从不拍照——透明背景上，连影子都是画的。姜片倒是很诚实的配角，辣得很坦然。
food-sushi.en: A sushi platter on a black wooden tray: salmon nigiri, tuna rolls and tamago each holding a corner, with wasabi and pickled ginger alongside. Plated as if for an advert, though it is never photographed — on a transparent background even the shadow is drawn. The ginger is an honest supporting actor, pungent without apology.

food-hotpot.zh: 红油火锅用黄铜九宫格锅，红汤底翻着辣椒与肉片、菇蔬，热气一腾起来就把整张图都暖了。规矩：格子要留着空位——吃到最后那几格往往是别人的。透明背景上汤不会凉，辣也不会减半分。
food-hotpot.en: A spicy hot pot in a brass nine-grid pot, red broth carrying peppers, meat slices and mushrooms and greens, steam rising until the whole picture warms. Rule: leave the grid spaces empty — the last few squares are usually someone else's. On a transparent background the broth never cools and the heat never eases.

food-skewer.zh: 孜然烤串是几根铁签串起焦香羊肉块，撒满孜然辣椒，旁边配着青葱。肉块边缘焦得发黑，油光还在。签子被握得发亮，说明有人已经决定要吃了——但透明背景上没人来，签子只好一直举着。
food-skewer.en: Several metal skewers of charred lamb cubes dusted with cumin and chili, scallions beside. The edges of the meat blacken, the sheen of fat still there. The skewers are polished bright by a grip, meaning someone already decided to eat — but on a transparent background nobody comes, so the skewer stays raised.

food-wonton.zh: 鲜虾云吞面是清汤碗里的三只云吞配细面，缀着小白菜和葱花，热气袅袅往上飘。云吞皮薄得能透出里面粉红的虾仁。规矩：一共三只，先吃哪只自己定——但吃下去就没了，碗永远是满的。
food-wonton.en: Three shrimp wontons and thin noodles in clear broth with bok choy and scallion, wisps of steam curling up. The wonton skins are thin enough to show the pink shrimp inside. Rule: there are three, and you choose which to eat first — except that eating one changes nothing, because the bowl stays full.

food-mapo.zh: 麻婆豆腐盛在白瓷碗里，红亮得发油，撒着青蒜与花椒，旁点一小撮肉末。麻辣是它的脾气，也是它的规矩——花椒点到刚好，不多不少。透明背景上豆腐不冒热气，只是看着像冒了。
food-mapo.en: Mapo tofu in a white bowl, glossy red, scattered with scallion and Sichuan peppercorn, a small mound of minced meat beside. The heat is its temperament and its rule — the peppercorn lands exactly right, no more and no less. On a transparent background the tofu gives off no heat, only looks as if it does.

toy-diabolo.zh: 空竹是两只竹轮并排的古老陀螺，轮面点着朱红与靛蓝旋纹，轮轴牵一根彩绳，绳头系一枚小铜铃。竹皮泛黄，细密裂纹像老人手上的纹。技巧在于抖：抖对了它自己会站住，抖错了就一头栽在透明背景上，再也起不来。
toy-diabolo.en: A diabolo of two bamboo wheels side by side, wheel faces dotted with vermilion and indigo spirals, a coloured cord through the axle with a tiny brass bell at the end. The bamboo skin has yellowed, fine cracks like the lines on an old hand. The whole skill lies in the wrist: whipped right, it stands on its own; whipped wrong, it falls onto the transparent background and never gets up.

toy-spinningtop.zh: 陀螺是车木削成的圆锥，顶端一截细杆可以捻在指间，锥身刷着靛蓝与朱红相间的旋纹，底端钉一枚磨亮的铁尖。木纹清晰，有几道开裂。它转到最后总要歪一下——那一下是它跟透明背景告别的动作。
toy-spinningtop.en: A lathe-turned wooden top, a slim peg at the crown for flicking between the fingers, its cone painted in indigo and vermilion spirals, a polished iron point at the base. The wood grain runs clear, with a few splits. At the very end it must lean once — that lean is how it says goodbye to the transparent background.

toy-jianzi.zh: 毽子以一枚方孔铜钱作底座，插上削好的鸡毛根，羽毛分红、黄、白三色分层散开。铜钱磨得发亮，边上还留着一点绿锈。踢得好的时候它能立在空中不落，踢不好就趴在透明背景上，羽毛还是照样分三层。
toy-jianzi.en: A jianzi built on a square-holed coin base fitted with trimmed rooster quills, plumage fanning out in layers of red, yellow and white. The coin is worn bright with a touch of verdigris at the edge. Kicked well it can stand in the air without falling; kicked badly it lies down on the transparent background with its feathers still neatly layered.

toy-kite.zh: 沙燕风筝是北京式燕子造型，竹篾骨架撑出双翼与尖尾，糊上薄纸后点上靛青、朱红与藤黄的几笔，尾梢垂两条飘带。纸面带细微折痕，是被风反复折过又展开留下的。它飞得越高，线越难放——规矩是放线的人不能抬头太久。
toy-kite.en: A Beijing swallow kite, bamboo splints stretched into two wings and a pointed tail, covered in thin paper and brushed with a few strokes of indigo, vermilion and rattan yellow, two ribbons trailing from the tail tip. Fine creases run across the paper, folded and unfolded by wind. The higher it flies, the harder the line pulls — rule: whoever holds it must not look up for long.

toy-lantern.zh: 走马灯是六棱纸罩灯笼，内壁装一圈可转的纸轮，轮上剪出人马花鸟的剪影。罩面画着折枝花卉，烛光把暖黄透出来，纸骨竹圈在光里分明。它转一圈，人马就走过一圈——透明的背景上那些剪影，谁也追不上。
toy-lantern.en: A hexagonal paper-shade lantern holding a rotating drum lined with cut-out silhouettes of riders, birds and flowers. The shade is painted with blossoming branches and lit from within by a warm candle glow, bamboo hoops showing crisply through. Each turn carries the riders one circuit of the drum — and on a transparent background, nobody ever catches them.

toy-ninerings.zh: 九连环由九枚铜环串在一根弯钩铜杆上，环面磨出温润包浆，钩头铸成小如意头，环与环层层相扣。要解开它得按固定次序来，一步错，前面全白解。规矩：解开了也别急着得意——重新套回去才是本事。
toy-ninerings.en: Nine bronze rings threaded onto a curved bronze rod, ring faces worn to a warm patina, the hook cast as a small ruyi head, each ring nested into the next. It opens only in a fixed order; one wrong step undoes all the others. Rule: even when you crack it, don't crow — putting it back together is the real trick.

toy-tangram.zh: 七巧板是七块彩漆薄木板拼成的方形：两块大三角、三块中三角、两块小三角与一块平行四边形。板面漆色分朱红、靛蓝、藤黄、墨绿，边缘见浅色木茬。它能被拼成无数图形，但只有七块——想加东西是加不进来的。
toy-tangram.en: A tangram assembled into a square from seven painted wooden pieces — two large triangles, three medium, two small and a parallelogram — in vermilion, indigo, rattan yellow and ink green, pale wood showing at the cut edges. It can be arranged into countless figures, but there are only seven pieces — you cannot add a single one more.

toy-lubanlock.zh: 鲁班锁是六根木条互相咬合成的立体锁，榫头层层穿插，拆不开。竹节木面刷成深浅两色棕，边角磨出圆润包浆。它是这一组里唯一被设计成要拆的玩具——只不过要先学会装回去。规矩：拆到最后六根木条，你得能原样拼回。
toy-lubanlock.en: A Luban lock of six wooden bars mortised into an interlocking solid puzzle that cannot be pulled apart, bamboo-node wood stained in two shades of brown, corners worn to a rounded polish. It is the only toy here designed to be taken apart — though you must first learn to put it back. Rule: when you are down to six bars, you must be able to rebuild them as they were.

toy-pelletdrum.zh: 拨浪鼓是双面蒙皮的小鼓，左右各伸一柄，鼓面画着胖娃娃与牡丹，两粒木珠连着细绳绕在柄上。鼓身朱红，鼓框浅木色带着磨痕。摇起来两粒珠子轮流敲打，声音一左一右像在对话。规矩：它只能聊两句，多了就吵。
toy-pelletdrum.en: A pellet drum with skin stretched over both faces, a handle on each side, the drumheads painted with a plump child and peonies, two wooden beads on strings looped around the handles. Vermilion body, pale wooden rim worn smooth. Shaken, the two beads take turns striking, the sound alternating left and right like a conversation. Rule: it only manages two lines before it turns into noise.

toy-tumbler.zh: 不倒翁是个圆胖白娃娃，脑袋大身子短，穿红肚兜扎着小褡裢，圆底压着重心，推倒多少次都能自己晃回来。腮边两团红晕，表情憨笑。它不站得住也不需要站得住——规矩是：能弹回来的，都算站得稳。
toy-tumbler.en: A round chubby doll with an oversized head and short body, wearing a red belly band and a little waist pouch, its weighted round base making it wobble back upright however often it is pushed. Two rosy circles on the cheeks and a guileless grin. It cannot stand still and does not need to — rule: whatever can bounce back counts as standing firm.

toy-paperflip.zh: 纸翻花是用彩纸剪叠成的花形玩具，一拉一松便翻转开合，花瓣分靛蓝、朱红与藤黄多层。纸面薄透，折痕与剪刀毛边都看得见。规矩：拉绳的手不能抖，抖一下这朵花就散了，散了就得重新剪。
toy-paperflip.en: A paper flip flower cut and folded from coloured paper so it opens and turns as the string is pulled, layered petals in indigo, vermilion and rattan yellow. The paper is thin enough to see through, fold lines and scissor feathering both visible. Rule: do not let your hand shake on the string — one tremor and the flower comes apart, and then it must be cut again.

toy-bamboodragonfly.zh: 竹蜻蜓是竹刀削成的叶片插在木杆顶端，缠一根棉线，拨动后叶片旋起停在半空。竹片青黄相间带着毛刺，杆头缠线处磨出深色。它停在空中那一瞬最像蜻蜓——只一瞬，然后落下，再等下一次拨动。
toy-bamboodragonfly.en: A bamboo dragonfly, a shaved leaf blade fitted to the top of a wooden stick with a cotton cord wound around it, spun by hand until the blade hovers overhead. The blade alternates yellow-green with raw splinters, the cord seat darkened by wear. The moment it hangs in the air is the most dragonfly-like it will ever be — one moment, then down, waiting for the next spin.

toy-pinwheel.zh: 风车是四片斜折彩纸装在细竹签上，红黄蓝绿四色交叠成一圈风叶，转起来像一朵转动的花。纸边有折痕和轻微毛口。做它的人手笨，折得不太齐，转起来就有点晃——规矩：歪着转也算转。
toy-pinwheel.en: A pinwheel of four diagonally folded coloured papers pinned on a slender bamboo stick, red, yellow, blue and green overlapping into a ring of vanes that turns like a blossoming flower. The paper edges are creased and slightly feathered. Whoever folded it was clumsy, so it turns a little unevenly — rule: a crooked spin is still a spin.

toy-clothtiger.zh: 布老虎是棉布缝的虎头，额头一个黑底金线的王字，两耳圆立，颊边绣着虎纹，胡须用白线一根根挑出。橙黄棉布起了毛球，线头有点松。它早就被摸得起了球——规矩：这样的虎才值得留着，硬挺的新虎反而没人要。
toy-clothtiger.en: A cloth tiger head sewn from cotton, a gold-on-black 王 character stitched on the forehead, two round upright ears, tiger stripes embroidered along the cheeks, white thread whiskers pulled out one by one. The orange cotton has gone puffy and a few threads have loosened. It has been petted into fluff — rule: a tiger like that is worth keeping; a stiff new one nobody wants.

toy-rabbitlord.zh: 兔儿爷是北京庙会的泥塑兔神，长耳竖起，穿金黄甲胄蹬云纹翘头靴，双手捧着一面小旗。彩绘剥落露出白坯胎。它是庙会上的神像，却一点也不严肃——规矩：供完它就下桌，跟别的小玩意儿挤在一块儿玩。
toy-rabbitlord.en: The clay rabbit lord of Beijing temple fairs, long ears standing up, dressed in golden armour and cloud-patterned boots with turned-up toes, both hands holding a small banner. The paint has chipped back to the pale clay body. A temple-fair god who is in no way solemn — rule: once the offerings are done he comes down off the table and plays with everything else.

toy-nigugu.zh: 泥咕咕是胶泥捏的小鸟哨，胖身短尾，翅膀一捏就响，脊背刷红绿两色，尾根留一个空哨孔。泥胎干裂出细小裂纹。它其实有两副嗓子——捏翅膀是吱声，含着吹是长音。规矩：别对着别人的耳朵吹。
toy-nigugu.en: A nigugu clay bird whistle, plump body and short tail, its wing squeezing out a squeak, the back painted in red and green, a hollow whistle hole left at the base of the tail. The dried clay has cracked with fine fissures. It actually has two voices — squeeze the wing for a squeak, blow with it held for a long note. Rule: do not blow it near someone else's ear.

toy-sugarfigure.zh: 糖人是熬化的麦芽糖趁热吹成的糖画，琥珀通透带上糖丝的细纹，塑成举着花枪的小猴。糖体薄处近乎透明。它活得极短——糖会返潮，纹路会慢慢化掉。规矩：画的时候手要快，慢了糖就拉不动丝了。
toy-sugarfigure.en: A sugar figurine, maltose syrup boiled hot and blown into a sugar painting, amber and translucent with fine threads of pulled sugar, shaped into a small monkey raising a flowered spear. The thinnest parts are almost clear. It lives very briefly — sugar sweats and the lines slowly dissolve. Rule: the hand must be fast while it is drawn, or the syrup will not pull.

toy-klotski.zh: 华容道是木框棋盘里卡着一批红蓝滑块，块面画着武将与兵卒，四四方方严丝合缝。木框榫接紧密，带磨亮的包浆。规矩：块不能硬推——每次只许动空格旁边那一块，多推一步就卡死。
toy-klotski.en: A Klotski board where a crowd of red and blue sliding blocks painted with generals and soldiers is jammed tight inside a wooden frame, the pieces squared off and fitting snugly, the mortised frame rubbed to a mellow polish. Rule: no shoving — only the block beside the gap may move, and one push too many jams the whole thing.

toy-slingshot.zh: 弹弓是天然竹叉削成的 Y 形，叉尖各拴一段旧皮筋，兜里放着一颗圆泥丸。竹皮青褐带雀斑，握柄处汗渍磨得发亮。它其实不常打鸟，多半是打罐子、打树梢上的果子。规矩：橡皮筋绷紧的时候别站得太近。
toy-slingshot.en: A slingshot carved from a natural bamboo fork into a Y, an old rubber band looped around each fork tip, a round clay pellet resting in the pouch. The bamboo skin is greenish brown with mottled speckles, the grip polished by sweaty palms. It rarely hunts birds — mostly tin cans, or fruit still up in the branches. Rule: do not stand close while the band is drawn back.

toy-zongren.zh: 鬃人是天津胡同里的提线泥偶，骑在彩漆木马上，马颈扎一圈马尾鬃，小人穿红袄蓝裤，底座两只竹轮一拉就走。泥胎彩绘磨得斑驳，露出的底色已经分不清原本是什么红。它是骑在马上又被线牵着——规矩：算它是马上的兵，不算它是马上的囚犯。
toy-zongren.en: A string-pulled clay figure from a Tianjin alley, riding a painted wooden horse whose neck is bound with a mane of real horsehair, the little rider in a red jacket and blue trousers, two bamboo wheels on the base that roll when the strings are pulled. The clay and paint are rubbed mottled and the original colours can no longer be told apart. It rides a horse while also being led by strings — rule: count it as a soldier on horseback, not a prisoner on one.

kid-diabolo.zh: 抖空竹的男孩穿蓝灰短褂，双手扯着棉线把红金双轮甩到半空，一腿抬起，脸笑得眼睛都弯了。轮子转起来带风，线在阳光里抖成一条虚影。规矩：线一松他就得追着跑——所以玩这个的男孩，鞋总是跑掉一只。
kid-diabolo.en: A boy in a blue-grey short jacket working a diabolo on a cotton string, one leg lifted, the red-and-gold double wheel spinning between the cords, round face creased into a laugh. The wheel hums as it turns and the string blurs in the light. Rule: let the string slack and he has to run after it — which is why boys who play this always lose one shoe.

kid-jianzi.zh: 踢毽子的女孩穿红袄绿裤梳着双髻，抬起一脚把红羽毽子翻在半空，两臂张开保持平衡，衣摆随动作鼓起来。毽子在透明背景上飞得比哪都高，也落得比哪都准——它总往她脚背上落。
kid-jianzi.en: A girl in a red jacket and green trousers with two buns, kicking a jianzi so the red-feathered shuttlecock flips overhead, arms spread for balance and hem ballooning with the motion. It flies higher here than anywhere, and lands more surely too — it always comes down toward her instep.

kid-kite.zh: 放沙燕风筝的小童穿黄马甲暗蓝裤，仰着头，一手举线轴一手牵线，红黑彩绘的沙燕在身侧斜着打旋。线绷出一道细弧，风筝顺着线转，像被拴住的鸟。规矩：线不能放太长，长了孩子就管不住它了。
kid-kite.en: A small child in a yellow vest and dark blue trousers looking up while flying a sand-swallow kite, one hand raising the spool and the other holding the taut line, the red-and-black painted swallow banking beside them. The line bows into a thin arc and the kite turns along it like a tethered bird. Rule: do not let out too much line — past a certain length the child loses control of it.

kid-lantern.zh: 捧走马灯的女孩穿粉袄格纹罩衫梳着双髻，双手捧一盏走马灯，菱格纸窗里透出暖黄烛光，灯檐垂着短穗。她低着头看得认真，烛影在纸上慢慢转。规矩：灯举久了手会酸，所以这类小孩走路慢——她是在等纸轮转完一圈。
kid-lantern.en: A girl in a pink quilted jacket with two buns cradling a revolving paper lantern in both hands, warm candlelight glowing through the diamond-latticed windows, short tassels hanging from the eaves. Head bent in quiet concentration as the shadows turn slowly on the paper. Rule: holding a lantern tires the arms, so children like her walk slowly — they are waiting for the drum to finish its turn.

kid-drum.zh: 摇拨浪鼓的小男孩穿米色短褐蓝裤，把鼓摇得张嘴笑。鼓面朱红，两侧红球甩成两道弧线，一脚踮起跟着节奏晃。声音一左一右，像有两个人在替他说笑。规矩：他笑得停不下来的时候，多半是鼓快散了。
kid-drum.en: A little boy in a tan short coat and blue trousers shaking a pellet drum with a wide-open laugh, the drum face vermilion and its two red beads swinging out in arcs, one foot tiptoeing to the rhythm. The sound alternates left and right, like two people laughing on his behalf. Rule: when he cannot stop laughing, the drum is usually coming apart.

kid-top.zh: 抽陀螺的男孩穿灰蓝上衣棕裤，蹲着身子一手举细竹鞭杆，绳梢正甩向地上那只红蓝陀螺。他身子前倾眯着眼瞄，嘴里咬着气。规矩：陀螺一歪就得立刻再抽一鞭——手慢半拍，陀螺就躺在透明背景上不起来了。
kid-top.en: A boy in a slate-blue jacket and brown trousers crouching to whip a spinning top, one hand raising a slender bamboo whip as the cord lashes toward the red-and-blue top on the ground. He leans in with narrowed eyes, breath held. Rule: the moment the top starts to lean, whip again at once — half a beat slow and it lies down on the transparent background for good.

lil-scholar.zh: 书生穿素蓝长衫，衣缘绣着云纹，双手捧一卷书垂目沉思。云纹绣得很密，像一场没下完的雨。他走路极轻，怕吵醒书里的人。规矩：书卷不能展开太久——展开久了，里面的道理会跑到肩膀上去。
lil-scholar.en: The scholar wears a pale-blue robe with cloud-scroll hems and holds a rolled scroll in both hands, eyes lowered in calm thought. The cloud pattern is stitched so densely it looks like rain that never finished. He walks very quietly, for fear of waking whoever is in the book. Rule: do not keep the scroll open too long — left open, its meaning climbs up into your shoulders.

lil-tea.zh: 茶人穿棉麻宽袍，袖口衣缘染着水波纹，双手把茶盏捧在胸前，恬淡含笑。水波纹只在袖口那一圈，像他连喝茶的姿势都记得省水。他一天只喝三盏，多一盏就误了时辰。规矩：三盏之后别劝——劝了也是白劝。
lil-tea.en: The tea person wears a loose undyed-linen tunic with water-ripple motifs at the cuffs and cradles a tea cup at the chest, a tranquil composed smile. The ripples circle only the cuffs, as if even his posture remembered to save water. He drinks three cups a day; a fourth would ruin the hour. Rule: after the third, do not persuade him — it is wasted effort.

lil-embroider.zh: 绣娘穿交领襦裙，衣襟与腰带织着缠枝花纹，抬手引着线，偏头带一点俏皮神采。缠枝纹顺着腰带一路爬，爬到袖口就停住。她手里的线永远比绣完的活多出一截——规矩：线不要剪断，留着，下一件衣服就有得接。
lil-embroider.en: The embroiderer wears a fitted cross-collar ruqun with intertwined floral-vine patterns on the bodice and sash, a raised needle and trailing thread, her head tilted with a lively, slightly mischievous look. The vine climbs the sash and stops at the cuff. The thread in her hand is always longer than the work she has finished — rule: never cut the thread, keep it, so the next garment has something to join onto.

lil-sword.zh: 侠客穿短打劲装，护肩与袖口绘着方正雷纹，腰悬长剑，一手叉在腰带上，笑容不羁。雷纹画得方方正正，像他这个人。剑不轻，他从不觉得重——规矩：侠客不解释自己为什么拔剑，解释了就不侠了。
lil-sword.en: The swordsman wears a short practical martial outfit with bold angular thunder-key patterns on the shoulder guards, a sheathed sword at the hip, one hand on his belt and a roguish grin. The thunder pattern is square and blunt, like the man himself. The sword is not light and he never minds — rule: a swordsman never explains why he drew his blade; explain and he stops being one.

lil-music.zh: 琴师穿飘逸长衣，袖上散布星纹与卷草，斜抱一把古琴，仰首出神。他的琴横在胸前却没弹——他正听着什么。星纹只在袖口聚成一片，像他心里那点光。规矩：琴师抬头的瞬间别打断他，那是曲子最要紧的地方。
lil-music.en: The musician wears a flowing long robe with scattered star-and-scrolling-vine motifs on the sleeves, a small zither held diagonally, his gaze lifted and distant. The zither lies across his chest unplayed — he is listening to something. The stars gather only at the cuffs, like the light inside him. Rule: when the musician lifts his head, do not interrupt; that is where the piece turns.

lil-craft.zh: 匠人穿工装短褐，皮围裙上印着利落的方格纹，手里一把木刨，神情专注。围裙上的格子方方正正，跟他刨出来的木面一样。他做事不说话，一句多余的话能毁掉一刀。规矩：看他干活的时候别出声，出声就重来。
lil-craft.en: The craftsman wears a short work jacket and a leather apron printed with a crisp geometric grid, a small wooden plane in hand and an utterly focused face. The grid on the apron is as square as the boards he planes. He works without speaking; one unnecessary word can spoil a single cut. Rule: watch him work in silence — speak, and it starts again.

lil-merchant.zh: 掌柜穿圆领袍，领口衣缘缀着钱纹菱格，抬手像在议价，笑得精明又热络。菱格在领口排成一圈，像算盘珠子。规矩：跟他还价可以，但一次只能让一步——让多了他不赚，反而不再理你。
lil-merchant.en: The shopkeeper wears a round-collar gown with diamond-coin motifs along the collar and hem, one hand raised mid-gesture as if closing a deal, bright shrewd friendly smile. The diamonds line up at the collar like beads on an abacus. Rule: you may bargain with him, but concede one step at a time — concede too much and he earns nothing and stops dealing with you.

lil-recluse.zh: 隐者穿素简道袍，衣摆爬满冰裂纹釉样，拄一根结绳杖，含着通透的笑。冰裂纹从下摆一路裂到袖口，像釉面裂开却不碎。他不说话时最清楚，一开口反而添乱。规矩：不懂就别问——问了他也答，只是答得更少。
lil-recluse.en: The recluse wears a simple straw-trimmed Taoist robe with ice-crack glaze patterns crawling up the hem, a knotted walking staff in hand and a wise, amused half-smile. The crackle runs from hem to cuff like glaze that broke without shattering. He is clearest when he is silent; speaking only muddies it. Rule: if you do not understand, do not ask — he would answer, but with fewer words.

lil2-fisher.zh: 渔父穿蓑衣斗笠，衣缘织着鳞纹，肩扛钓竿、腰悬鱼篓，含笑缓步。鳞纹一片片压着，像真的鱼鳞贴上去。他钓的鱼从不装进篓里——篓是空的，鱼在钩上。规矩：跟他走一段路，不许问钓到了几条。
lil2-fisher.en: The fisherman wears a straw rain cape and conical hat with fish-scale patterns woven into the hem, a bamboo rod slung over the shoulder and a fish basket at the hip, strolling with a content smile. The scales lie one over another like real fish scales pressed on. His basket is always empty — the fish are on the hook. Rule: walk with him a while, and do not ask how many he has caught.

lil2-woodman.zh: 樵夫穿粗布短褐，胸前印着年轮纹，背负柴捆、肩扛长斧，咧嘴憨笑。年轮纹一圈套一圈，像他数过的树。柴捆压得肩膀歪，他也不换边。规矩：斧子落下之前别喊他——喊了斧头会偏。
lil2-woodman.en: The woodcutter wears a short work jacket with tree-ring patterns on the chest, a bundle of firewood on his back and a broad axe on his shoulder, a simple cheerful grin. The rings circle inside circles, like the trees he has counted. The bundle bends his shoulder and he never switches it. Rule: do not shout before the axe falls — shout, and the swing goes wide.

lil2-farmer.zh: 农夫穿粗布短衫，衣缘袖口绣着稻穗纹，扶着锄头抬手拭汗，头戴草帽，笑得温厚。稻穗纹沉甸甸地垂在袖口，穗子都朝一个方向。他一年种的东西自己吃不完。规矩：别问他收成——他会把最好的分给你。
lil2-farmer.en: The farmer wears a rough-spun tunic with golden rice-ear motifs on the hem and cuffs, leaning on a hoe and wiping his brow under a straw hat, warm good-natured smile. The ears hang heavy at the cuffs, all leaning the same way. He grows more than he can eat. Rule: do not ask about his harvest — he will hand you the best of it.

lil2-cowherd.zh: 牧童穿短衣短裤，肩头印着柳叶纹，横笛吹奏，赤脚而立，歪头俏笑。柳叶纹被风吹得动，纹样也跟着动。他吹的调子只有一句，吹第二遍时自己先笑了。规矩：笛声一停就别说要听——他吹第二遍会更好。
lil2-cowherd.en: The cowherd boy wears short pants and an open shirt with willow-leaf motifs on the shoulders, playing a bamboo flute barefoot, head tilted with a mischievous grin. The willow leaves seem to stir, and the pattern with them. His tune is a single phrase, and the second time through he laughs before it ends. Rule: when the flute stops, do not ask for an encore — the second time through is better.

lil2-healer.zh: 郎中穿洗练长衫，胸前绣着灵芝纹，背着药箱，手里托着药杵，含笑伸手。灵芝纹一圈圈绕在胸口，像长年采药的路线。他递药时总先递最不苦的那味。规矩：问他治不治得好——他只会说：先吃。
lil2-healer.en: The healer wears a long pale robe with lingzhi mushroom motifs across the chest, a medicine chest on his back and a small mortar in hand, offering a remedy with a compassionate smile. The lingzhi rings circle his chest like the routes of years spent gathering herbs. He always offers the least bitter medicine first. Rule: ask him whether it will work — he will only say: take it first.

lil2-taoist.zh: 道士穿深蓝道袍，胸前缀一枚八卦纹圆章，拂尘搭在小臂上，垂目淡然。八卦章上的卦爻磨得看不清一半。他从不说自己会什么，只说今日不宜。规矩：他说不宜的事就别做——他一年里说错的次数，一只手数得完。
lil2-taoist.en: The Taoist wears a dark-blue robe with a circular bagua medallion on the chest, a horsetail whisk across the forearm, eyes gently lowered. Half the trigrams on the medallion have worn past reading. He never says what he can do, only that today is unsuitable. Rule: do not do the things he calls unsuitable — the number of times he is wrong in a year can be counted on one hand.

lil2-monk.zh: 僧侣穿橙黄僧衣，衣缘缀着莲瓣纹，腕上绕一串念珠，手里托一只陶钵，垂目浅笑。莲瓣纹一瓣一瓣从下摆开上去，像在慢慢长。他托钵的手很稳——钵里没有饭，他照样托着。规矩：钵前别站太久，他不催人，但你会自己不好意思。
lil2-monk.en: The monk wears a saffron robe with lotus-petal motifs along the hem, prayer beads at the wrist and an alms bowl in hand, serene lowered eyes. The petals open upward one by one from the hem, as though still growing. His hand is steady, though the bowl is empty — he carries it all the same. Rule: do not stand too long before the bowl; he will not rush you, but you will embarrass yourself.

lil2-warrior.zh: 武生穿紧身扎甲，肩胸绘着腾起的火焰纹，长枪往地上一杵，另一手按拳而立，目光炯炯。火焰纹烧到领口就停住，没有一处烧过头。他亮相时不眨眼，亮相完了才眨。规矩：枪一旦杵下去，他不会再动第二下——除非你先动。
lil2-warrior.en: The martial performer wears a fitted armoured costume with bold flame patterns blazing up the shoulders, a long spear planted and a fist at the hip, intense blazing eyes. The flames reach the collar and stop there, not one stroke beyond. He holds the pose without blinking and only blinks once it is done. Rule: once the spear is planted, he will not move a second time — unless you move first.

lil2-poet.zh: 诗人穿青绿长衫，袖上垂着竹节纹，腰间挂一只酒壶，仰首吟哦，疏放一笑。竹节纹一节一节数下去，数到第七节就断了——那节是空出来的位置。他念完一句总要等半拍，像在等谁接。规矩：他等的那半拍，别接，他会自己续上。
lil2-poet.en: The poet wears a teal robe with bamboo-node motifs down the sleeves, a wine gourd at the waist, head tilted upward reciting verse with a proud, detached smile. The nodes are counted down and the seventh is blank — that gap is deliberate. After each line he waits half a beat, as if for someone to answer. Rule: do not fill that half-beat; he will continue by himself.

lil2-drinker.zh: 酒仙宽袍敞怀，襟口绣着旋涡纹，怀抱一只酒坛，醉眼眯笑，衣袖滑落半边。旋涡纹一圈套一圈，看久了会跟着转。他醉得很有分寸——从不超过三分，因为第四分就站不住了。规矩：想扶他的时候别扶，他会自己稳。
lil2-drinker.en: The wine immortal wears a loosely open robe with swirling spiral patterns on the lapels, hugging a wine jar, blissful tipsy grin, one sleeve slipping. The spirals spiral inside spirals, and after a while your eyes follow them. He is drunk with precision — never past the third measure, because the fourth is where standing fails. Rule: do not steady him if he stumbles; he will find his own feet.

lil2-goplayer.zh: 棋士穿宽袖深袍，衣缘织着棋格纹，指间拈着一枚棋子，敛袖而立，凝神静思。棋格纹方方正正，从衣摆一直排到袖口。他落子之前会把棋子在指间转三圈。规矩：不要在他数到第三圈时说话——第三圈之后就是落子。
lil2-goplayer.en: The go player wears a wide-sleeved dark robe with a subtle grid motif at the hem, a single stone pinched between his fingers, half-closed eyes in concentration. The grid runs square from hem to cuff. Before placing a stone he turns it in his fingers three times. Rule: do not speak as he counts the third turn — after the third, the stone falls.

lil2-painter.zh: 画师穿飘逸长衫，肩头绕着卷云纹，执笔悬腕，一手半卷画纸，回眸带笑。卷云纹在肩头绕成一个小旋涡，像他脑子里的主意。他落笔前先在空中比划两下，那两下才是画。规矩：别催他——画没出来之前，画纸只是一张纸。
lil2-painter.en: The painter wears a flowing gown with scrolling-cloud motifs across the shoulders, a fine brush aloft, a half-unrolled paper in the other hand, glancing back with a lively smile. The clouds coil into a small swirl at the shoulder, like an idea turning over. He traces two shapes in the air before he commits — those two strokes are the picture. Rule: do not rush him; before the picture exists, the paper is only paper.

lil2-gardener.zh: 花匠穿短衣围裙，围裙上印着宝相花纹，臂弯挎一只花篮，手里拿着花剪，俯身含笑。宝相花纹一圈圈绕在围裙上，像一朵永远开着的花。他剪枝时先比一比，才下剪。规矩：他比的时候别凑近看——花剪很准，比的时间是留给花的。
lil2-gardener.en: The gardener wears a work apron printed with ornate baoxiang floral medallions, a basket of blooms on one arm and flower shears in the other, bending in with a warm smile. The medallions circle the apron like a flower that never closes. He measures a branch before he cuts. Rule: do not lean in while he measures — the shears are accurate, and the measuring is for the flower.

lil2-boatman.zh: 艄公穿粗布短褂，衣缘印着江崖纹，撑篙而立，一手搭在额前远望，咧嘴憨笑，牙都看得见。江崖纹从衣摆叠上来，一层压一层，像远处的山。他一天来回十几趟，篙上的手印比脸还黑。规矩：船靠岸时别催，他先把船停稳。
lil2-boatman.en: The boatman wears a coarse short jacket with jagged river-cliff wave motifs at the hem, gripping a punt pole, one hand shading his eyes to the distance, broad gap-toothed grin. The cliffs stack upward from the hem like far mountains. He makes a dozen trips a day, and his hands on the pole are darker than his face. Rule: do not rush him at the landing — he stops the boat first.

lil2-hunter.zh: 猎人穿皮质猎装，肩头缀着鹿角纹，背负弯弓、腰悬箭囊，搭手远眺，目光锐利。鹿角纹在肩上一分岔，岔口都朝着他看的方向。他的弓背在背上，箭在囊里，一直没动过。规矩：他不打已经看见的——他要等它自己再往前走一步。
lil2-hunter.en: The hunter wears a fitted leather hunting outfit with deer-antler motifs on the shoulder, a recurve bow on his back and a quiver at the hip, keen scanning gaze. The antlers fork at the shoulder, both tines pointing where he is looking. His bow stays on his back and his arrows stay in the quiver, unmoved. Rule: he does not shoot what he already sees — he waits for it to take one more step.

lil2-herbalist.zh: 采药人扎着巾，穿短褐，袖缘印草叶纹，背一只竹篓，手里拈着一枝细看，神情专注。草叶纹顺着袖缘往上长，长到肩头就断了——再往上是山，不是衣服。他分不清草和菜，但分得出哪一枝不能采。规矩：跟着他走可以，别伸手碰他筐里的。
lil2-herbalist.en: The herbalist wears a tied headcloth and short tunic with herb-leaf vein motifs on the sleeves, a bamboo basket of plants on his back, closely examining a sprig, quiet and absorbed. The leaf veins climb the sleeve and stop at the shoulder — beyond that is mountain, not clothing. He cannot tell grass from vegetables, but he can tell which sprig must not be picked. Rule: walk with him if you like, but do not reach into his basket.

lil2-diviner.zh: 卜者穿宽大深袍，胸前缀着龟甲纹，一手持幡，一手捧龟甲，眯眼诡笑。龟甲上的裂纹纵横交错，像一张看不懂的地图。他给人指路之前从不看路，只看甲。规矩：别问他算得准不准——他只说：甲上是这么写的。
lil2-diviner.en: The diviner wears a wide dark robe with hexagonal tortoise-shell patterns across the chest, a banner staff in one hand and an ancient cracked shell in the other, enigmatic narrowed smile. The cracks cross and recross like an unreadable map. Before pointing anyone anywhere, he never looks at the road, only at the shell. Rule: do not ask how accurate he is — he says only: the shell says so.

lil2-flutist.zh: 笛者穿飘逸长衣，袖缘旋着风回纹，横笛闭目，广袖临风，身姿若悬。风回纹一圈圈顺着袖口转，转到袖尖就散开。他吹的调子在透明背景上听得见风，却看不见风。规矩：他闭眼的时候别拍手——他会换一段更轻的。
lil2-flutist.en: The flutist wears a flowing long robe with curling wind-spiral motifs along the sleeves, a bamboo flute to the lips, eyes closed, wide sleeves in the air, weightless poise. The spirals travel down the sleeve and scatter at the tip. You can hear the wind in his tune on a transparent background, but you cannot see it. Rule: do not applaud while his eyes are closed — he will switch to something softer.

lil2-lady.zh: 仕女穿交领襦裙，裙裾缀着团花纹，执扇半掩面，敛袖低眉，步摇轻晃。团花纹一朵一朵圆得规矩，藏在裙褶里。她笑的时候扇子会挡掉一半——看得到的那一半才是给你看的。规矩：她把扇子放下的时候再走近半步，那才是真的。
lil2-lady.en: The classical lady wears an elegant cross-collar ruqun with round floral medallions on the skirt, a silk fan half concealing her face, head gently lowered, a hairpin swaying. The medallions are perfectly round, hiding in the pleats. When she smiles the fan hides half of it — the visible half is the half meant for you. Rule: move closer only after she lowers the fan; only then is it real.

lil2-child.zh: 稚子穿红肚兜短裤，布上印着石榴纹，高高举起一串糖葫芦，赤脚雀跃，咧嘴大笑。石榴纹裂着口籽都露出来。他跑起来肚兜会歪，但从来不系紧——系紧了就不肯走路了。规矩：别扶他，他摔了自己会爬起来笑得更大声。
lil2-child.en: The little child wears a bright belly-band and shorts printed with pomegranate-burst motifs, a stick of candied haws held overhead, hopping barefoot with a big toothy grin. The pomegranates are split open, seeds showing. His belly-band slips as he runs and is never tied tight — tied tight, he refuses to walk. Rule: do not lift him; if he falls he gets up laughing harder.

emblem-cloudwhale.zh: 云中鲸是一头小蓝鲸游过卷起的象牙白云，云下悬着三颗雨滴，鲸背喷出一小缕雾气。深钴蓝圆底压着细金边框，上下各一枚小铆钉。它游过的云都不下雨——雨都被它背上那口气挡住了。
emblem-cloudwhale.en: A cloud whale swims through a curled ivory cloud, three raindrops hanging below and a curl of mist rising from its spout, on a deep cobalt enamel field inside a thin brass rim with two rivets. The clouds it passes never rain — the puff from its back holds the rain off.

emblem-bottledstorm.zh: 瓶中雷是一只琥珀玻璃小瓶封着朱红软木塞，瓶里关着一道盘成圈的金黄闪电，瓶颈浮着三点火星。深青绿圆底配细金边框。那道闪电在瓶里已经待了很多年，一直没等到要劈的那一下。
emblem-bottledstorm.en: A small amber glass bottle sealed with a coral cork, a coiled golden lightning bolt trapped inside and three sparks floating near the neck, on a deep teal enamel field inside a thin brass rim. That bolt has been in the bottle a long time and has still not found the strike it was waiting for.

emblem-hiveclock.zh: 蜂巢钟是八格蜜金蜂巢绕着中央一块象牙白钟面，钟面只有两根黄铜指针和十二颗小圆点，不留任何数字。两只小蜜蜂停在巢格上。指针照走，可谁也说不清它指几点——上面没有数字。
emblem-hiveclock.en: Eight honey-gold wax cells ring a blank ivory clock dial with only two brass hands and twelve tiny gold dots, no numerals at all, two small bees resting on the cells. The hands move, but nobody can say what hour it shows — there are no numbers to say it with.

emblem-eyekey.zh: 眼钥匙是一把立着的旧式铜钥匙，钥匙环化成一只睁开的绿眼睛，瞳孔居中，下方短短的睫毛正好排成钥匙齿。深墨绿圆底配细金边框。这把钥匙不开门——它只负责看。
emblem-eyekey.en: An upright old brass key whose bow becomes a wide open green eye with a dark pupil, short eyelashes forming the key teeth below, on a deep inky green enamel field inside a thin brass rim. This key opens no door — it is only in charge of looking.

emblem-windupplanet.zh: 发条行星是一颗薄荷绿带珊瑚红纹的小行星，斜套着黄铜星环，右侧伸出一枚上发条的钥匙。深靛蓝圆底撒着三颗象牙小星。它每转一圈要上一次弦——转得比钟快，但比钟累。
emblem-windupplanet.en: A pale mint planet streaked with coral red, tilted inside a warm brass ring, a wind-up key protruding from its right side, three ivory stars scattered over a midnight indigo field. It must be wound once per revolution — turning faster than a clock, but working harder than one.

emblem-mothcandle.zh: 蛾与烛是一支短铜烛台上的蜡烛，烧着高高的暖橙火苗，一只浅色飞蛾展翅绕着火转，两缕细烟盘上去。暗红圆底配细金边框。蛾子每晚都来，烧掉多少蜡它不在意——它只认那点光。
emblem-mothcandle.en: A candle in a short brass holder burning with a tall amber flame, one pale moth circling it with spread wings, two curls of smoke above, on a deep burnt-red enamel field inside a thin brass rim. The moth comes every night and does not care how much wax it costs — it only knows that light.

emblem-keyholegarden.zh: 锁孔花园里长出一座微型花园，圆头小树撑开黄绿树冠，三朵小花与卷须绕着树根，一架小梯子斜靠在锁孔内壁。土黄与苔绿圆底配细金边框。没人拿钥匙来开——这扇门是自己开的。
emblem-keyholegarden.en: A large ornate keyhole holding a miniature garden, a round little tree with a yellow-green canopy, three small flowers and curling tendrils at its roots, a tiny ladder leaning against the inner edge, on an ochre and moss-green field inside a thin brass rim. Nobody brings a key — this door opened itself.

emblem-moonsnail.zh: 月蜗是一只小蜗牛，背着象牙白月牙壳，壳上旋着细细的螺纹，头顶两枚软触角，身后跟着一颗小星与两点碎光。淡紫蓝圆底配细金边框。它背上的壳是月亮的边——月缺的那一块，正好够蜗牛住。
emblem-moonsnail.en: A small snail carrying an ivory crescent-moon shell with a fine spiral, two soft antennae on its head, one little star and two dots trailing behind, on a pale lavender blue field inside a thin brass rim. Its shell is the edge of the moon — the missing crescent is exactly room enough for a snail.

emblem-umbrellajelly.zh: 伞水母是一柄小阳伞，伞盖化作半透明水母，垂下的触须正好排成伞骨，周围落着三颗雨滴，伞柄弯出小钩。深靛蓝圆底配细金边框。下雨的时候它不躲——它就是雨伞。
emblem-umbrellajelly.en: A small parasol whose domed canopy is a translucent jellyfish, dangling tentacles forming the umbrella ribs, three raindrops falling around it and a tiny curled handle below, on a deep indigo field inside a thin brass rim. When it rains it does not take shelter — it is the shelter.

emblem-teacupgalaxy.zh: 茶杯星河是一只白瓷小茶杯连着杯托，杯口旋出一圈细碎星河与淡蓝雾气，上方浮着三颗四角星。深青绿圆底配细金边框。杯里盛的小宇宙没别的客人，只在杯沿转一圈就走了。
emblem-teacupgalaxy.en: A small white porcelain teacup on its saucer with a swirl of tiny stars and pale blue mist rising from it, three four-pointed stars floating above, on a deep teal field inside a thin brass rim. The little galaxy in the cup has no other guests — it turns once around the rim and leaves.

emblem-matchboxfire.zh: 火柴盒篝火是一只半抽开的小火柴盒，盒里躺着两根火柴，敞开的盒屉上烧着一小簇交叉枝条的篝火，飘起一缕淡烟。深酒红圆底配细金边框。盒里的两根没点——留着下次再用。
emblem-matchboxfire.en: A small matchbox slid half open with two matches inside, a tiny campfire of crossed twigs burning above the open tray and one curl of pale smoke drifting up, on a deep wine red field inside a thin brass rim. The two matches inside are unlit — saved for next time.

emblem-bookbirds.zh: 书页飞鸟是一本摊开的空白书册，珊瑚红书封，三只折纸小鸟从书页间飞起，另有两页纸在上方打旋，页面上不留任何字迹。深墨绿圆底配细金边框。字被人一页页拿走了，剩下纸折成了鸟。
emblem-bookbirds.en: An open book with completely blank ivory pages and a coral red cover, three little origami paper birds flying up out of it and two loose pages fluttering above, no writing anywhere, on a deep forest green field inside a thin brass rim. Someone took the words away page by page, and folded the remainder into birds.

emblem-lanternfish.zh: 灯中小鱼是一盏黄铜小提灯，圆玻璃罩里游着一尾橙色小鱼，衬着两枝水草与三颗气泡，顶上带小提环。午夜蓝圆底配细金边框。鱼不游向灯芯——它只在这盏灯里绕圈。
emblem-lanternfish.en: A small brass hand lantern whose rounded glass chamber holds one tiny orange fish like an aquarium, two green water weeds and three bubbles around it, a short carrying loop on top, on a midnight blue field inside a thin brass rim. The fish never swims toward the flame — it only circles inside this lantern.

emblem-clocktree.zh: 齿轮树是一圈相扣的黄铜小齿轮围着中央一块象牙白空白圆盘，盘心长出一株三枝绿叶小树，两缕细根攀过盘沿。深赭褐圆底配细金边框。圆盘上没有指针也没有数字——这棵树自己就是时间。
emblem-clocktree.en: A ring of interlocking brass gear wheels around a completely blank ivory dial, a tiny green tree with three leafy branches growing from its centre and two roots curling over the edge, on a deep ochre brown field inside a thin brass rim. No hands, no numerals — the tree itself is the time.

emblem-keymoon.zh: 钥匙月是一把立着的旧式黄铜钥匙，圆环钥柄化作一弯象牙白月牙，细链上垂着两颗小星，下方是短短的钥匙齿。深紫圆底配细金边框。月亮挂在一把钥匙上，钥匙却打不开它。
emblem-keymoon.en: An upright old brass key whose round bow becomes a slender ivory crescent moon, two tiny four-pointed stars hanging from it on fine chains, short plain key teeth below, on a deep plum purple field inside a thin brass rim. A moon hangs from a key, and the key cannot open it.

emblem-bottlesail.zh: 瓶中帆是一只斜躺的透明玻璃瓶，素软木塞封口，瓶中一叶白三角帆小船浮在一小卷蓝浪上，瓶颈旁两颗气泡。深松绿圆底配细金边框。瓶身不贴任何标签也不塞纸条——那船自己认得路。
emblem-bottlesail.en: A small clear glass bottle lying at a slight angle with a plain cork stopper, a tiny white sailboat floating inside on a curl of blue wave and two bubbles near the neck, on a deep pine green field inside a thin brass rim. No label, no folded note inside — the boat knows the way by itself.

emblem-wellstars.zh: 井中星夜是一眼石砌小井的圆形井口，幽深井里藏着一小片夜空与三颗金星、一弯月牙，绳上吊着一只黄铜小桶。灰蓝石色圆底配细金边框。井里的星星不用打水——打水的人只管把桶放下去。
emblem-wellstars.en: The round stone rim of a little wishing well seen slightly from above, a miniature night sky with three golden stars and a small crescent moon inside its dark opening, a tiny brass bucket hanging on a rope, on a deep blue-gray slate field inside a thin brass rim. The stars in the well need no water drawn — whoever wants them simply lowers the bucket.

emblem-drawerspring.zh: 抽屉春天是一只带圆铜拉手的小木抽屉，被拉开一半，抽屉里长出一枝三朵花的花枝与两只小蝴蝶，几片绿叶翻过抽屉边沿。赤陶红圆底配细金边框。抽屉一直关着的时候，春天在里面等。
emblem-drawerspring.en: A small wooden drawer pulled half open with a round brass knob, a flowering branch with three blossoms and two little butterflies growing out of it, a few green leaves curling over the edge, on a deep terracotta red field inside a thin brass rim. As long as the drawer stays shut, the spring waits inside it.

emblem-telescopecomet.zh: 镜中彗星是一支短筒黄铜单筒望远镜斜指向上，宽镜口里探出一颗拖着长长卷尾的小彗星，镜口旁三颗碎星。深靛蓝圆底配细金边框。它被望远镜看见时，正在离开——所以永远只看得到尾巴。
emblem-telescopecomet.en: A short antique brass spyglass angled upward, a bright little comet with a long curling golden tail emerging from its wide front lens, three tiny stars around the lens, on a deep indigo blue field inside a thin brass rim. It is already leaving when the glass finds it — which is why only the tail is ever seen.

emblem-birdcagecloud.zh: 笼中云是一只带小顶环的黄铜鸟笼，笼门半开，笼里关着的不是鸟而是一朵三瓣蓬松白云，两颗小雨滴正从门缝溜出去。深墨绿圆底配细金边框。门是开的——云要出去，雨跟出去两滴。
emblem-birdcagecloud.en: An ornate brass birdcage with its little door swung open, one fluffy white cloud with three rounded lobes floating inside instead of a bird, two tiny raindrops escaping through the door, on a deep forest green field inside a thin brass rim. The door is open — the cloud is leaving, and two drops of rain go with it.

emblem-hourglassflower.zh: 沙漏花是一只黄铜框架小沙漏，上球装的是珊瑚色花瓣而不是沙，三片花瓣正穿过细颈落下，下球积成小小一堆。深紫圆底配细金边框。它漏的是花——落完一次要等很久才重新开满。
emblem-hourglassflower.en: A small hourglass with a brass frame, its upper bulb filled with loose coral flower petals instead of sand, three petals falling through the narrow neck and a little mound gathered below, on a deep plum purple field inside a thin brass rim. It leaks flowers — after one run it takes a long while to fill again.

emblem-doorsea.zh: 门里海是一扇圆顶小木门半掩着，门缝里涌出两卷蓝海浪与一叶白帆，门板上有一枚小锁孔，门前三级台阶。深青绿圆底配细金边框。门后不是房间——门后是海，门只是开在那儿。
emblem-doorsea.en: A small round-topped wooden door standing half open, two curling blue sea waves and one tiny white sailboat visible through the opening, a little brass keyhole and three small steps, on a deep teal field inside a thin brass rim. Behind the door is no room — behind it is the sea; the door simply stands there.

emblem-quillmoon.zh: 羽笔月是一支斜置的象牙白羽毛笔配金色笔尖，笔尖滴下一弯细月牙与三颗星形墨点，下方卷着一小缕墨涡。深酒红圆底配细金边框。写下的不是字，是能浮起来的东西。
emblem-quillmoon.en: One ivory feather quill angled diagonally with a golden nib, a slender crescent moon and three star-shaped ink droplets dripping from the nib, a tiny swirl of ink below, on a deep wine red field inside a thin brass rim. What it writes is not words — it is things that can float.

emblem-gearbfly.zh: 齿轮蝶是一只正面展翅的对称蝴蝶，翅面由相扣的小黄铜齿轮拼成，身体中央盘着一圈发条弹簧，两根卷曲触角，翅缘点着珊瑚小点。深赭褐圆底配细金边框。翅膀转起来时会响——很轻，但听得见。
emblem-gearbfly.en: A butterfly seen front-on with perfectly symmetrical wings made of small interlocking brass gears, a coiled clockwork spring at the centre of its body, two curled antennae and tiny coral dots along the wing edges, on a deep ochre brown field inside a thin brass rim. Its wings make a sound as they turn — very faint, but audible.

emblem-envelopeforest.zh: 信封森林是一只掀开封口的素色信封，里面长出三棵圆头小树与两朵小蘑菇，几片叶子和一根藤蔓翻过纸边，信封上不留地址、邮票或任何字迹。深松绿圆底配细金边框。没人寄它——它寄给自己。
emblem-envelopeforest.en: An opened plain envelope with its flap lifted, three tiny round trees and two small mushrooms growing out of it, a few leaves and a vine curling over the paper edge, completely blank with no address, stamp or writing, on a deep pine green field inside a thin brass rim. Nobody mailed it — it mails itself.

emblem-rainbulb.zh: 灯泡雨是一只黄铜螺口的大圆玻璃灯泡，玻璃里落着四颗淡蓝雨滴，底部积成小水洼泛起两圈涟漪，顶上浮着一小朵云。午夜蓝圆底配细金边框。灯泡不亮也没有任何印字——它只是一间很小的屋子，雨在里面下得刚好。
emblem-rainbulb.en: A large round glass light bulb with a brass screw base, a tiny shower of four pale blue raindrops falling inside into a small puddle with two ripple rings, one little cloud near the top, the bulb unlit with no markings, on a midnight blue field inside a thin brass rim. The bulb is not lit and bears no lettering — it is simply a very small room where it rains just right.

emblem-chesscastle.zh: 棋子城堡是一枚象牙白国际象棋车，做成三垛雉堞的小城堡塔，塔身两扇拱窗，顶上细铜杆挑着一面珊瑚小三角旗，宽圆底座。深蓝灰圆底配细金边框。棋子上没有任何字母或记号——它守的城不归任何一国。
emblem-chesscastle.en: One ivory chess rook shaped as a tiny castle tower with three crenellations, a small coral pennant on a thin brass pole, two arched windows and a wide round base, completely plain with no letters or markings, on a deep blue-gray slate field inside a thin brass rim. No letters, no marks — the castle it guards belongs to no country.

emblem-shellrecord.zh: 贝壳唱片是一枚左右对称张开的扇贝壳，壳心托着一张小黑胶唱片，中心圆标是象牙白空白一片，只有几圈素纹沟槽，旁边斜靠一枚黄铜音叉，上方三点碎光。赤陶红圆底配细金边框。唱片的中心标签是空的——唱的是什么，它不打算说。
emblem-shellrecord.en: An open scallop shell with two symmetrical fans holding a small gramophone record with a completely blank ivory centre label and plain concentric grooves, a little brass tuning fork leaning beside it and three tiny sparkles above, on a deep terracotta red field inside a thin brass rim. The label is blank — what it plays, it declines to say.

characters.zh: 本站人口第一大户。老张领着果克星人和一干漫画风小人住在这里，职责是给各类项目当立绘、当看板、当吉祥物。按图鉴规矩，他们都不露脸给摄像头看，只以透明 PNG 形态出门。
characters.en: The gallery's largest household. Led by Laozhang alongside the Guck aliens and a cast of comic-style figures, they serve as character art, mascots and poster faces. Per house rules they never face a camera — they only go out as transparent PNGs.

weapons.zh: 冷兵器与奇械的中间地带，每件都认真权衡过杀伤力与造型的平衡。事实证明，一把武器要想被记住，锤头比道理更重要。
weapons.en: The middle ground between cold steel and odd machinery, where every piece has weighed lethality against silhouette. A weapon, it turns out, is remembered for its head rather than its reasoning.

ammo.zh: 全站最没耐心的分类：存在的意义就是被用完。黄铜、底火与纸壳陈列在这里，纯属工伤。
ammo.en: The most impatient category on the site: their whole purpose is to be spent. Brass, primers and paper shells — displayed here purely as occupational injury.

animals.zh: 从黑猫到渡鸦，本站的动物一律不拆家，只负责在透明背景上维持体面。饲养它们不需要猫砂，需要的是 PNG 的 Alpha 通道。
animals.en: From black cats to ravens, the site's animals never wreck the house — they merely hold their composure on a transparent background. Keeping them requires no litter box, just a PNG alpha channel.

food.zh: 拉面、蛋糕、炒饭、寿司、火锅、烤串、云吞面、麻婆豆腐与可疑罐头。本站的食物永远停在刚出锅的完美瞬间，而且永远吃不到——这是图鉴的残忍之处。热气照升不误，脚下照投影，但透明背景上什么都不会留下。
food.en: Ramen, cake, fried rice, sushi, hot pot, skewers, wonton noodles, mapo tofu and tins of dubious content. The food here is forever at its perfect just-served moment, and forever inedible — such is the cruelty of a gallery. The steam rises on schedule, the shadow falls beneath, but nothing ever stays on a transparent background.

gizmos.zh: 六件巴掌大的黄铜小器械：自鸣座钟、多节机械手、喷汽风轮、自动研墨磨、折叠观星仪、发条八音匣。每一件都能动，但动得都不太可靠——铜壳发乌、刻痕纵横、铜绿点点，是常年摆弄留下的年轮。规矩：只看不摸，摸之前先想清楚它会不会突然响。
gizmos.en: Six palm-sized brass contraptions: a chiming clock, a jointed grabber, a steam whirligig, a self-grinding ink mill, a folding astrolabe and a clockwork music box. Every one of them moves, but none moves quite reliably — tarnished shells, fine scratches and spots of verdigris, the rings of a lifetime of handling. Rules: look, don't touch, and think twice before you touch, because something might start chiming.

alienleaves.zh: 八枚从别的世界飘来的叶子标本：星脉、晶格、齿轮、月相、灯脉、双螺、鳞甲、露镜。叶肉有深靛蓝、翡翠绿、酒红，每片都规规矩矩平铺在透明背景上，像一页植物图鉴活页。规矩：只收叶子，不收根——根一来，这一页就长不完了。
alienleaves.en: Eight leaf specimens blown in from elsewhere: star-veined, crystal-honeycombed, clockwork, moon-phased, lantern-veined, twin-spiralled, metal-scaled, dew-lensed. The blades run deep indigo, emerald and wine red, each one laid out flat and proper on a transparent background like a living page of a botanical atlas. Rules: leaves only, never roots — once the roots come, the page never ends.

emblems.zh: 三十枚别针大小的奇想徽章，每一枚都把一件不可能的事做成了一枚珐琅圆章：鲸在云里游、闪电被塞进瓶子、钟面长成蜂巢、钥匙长出眼睛、抽屉里抽出春天、灯泡里下着雨。构图一律居中对称，细金边框，上下各一枚小铆钉。规矩：徽章只讲一件事，讲不清楚就换一个想法。
emblems.en: Thirty curious emblems the size of a brooch, each turning one impossible thing into a single enamel disc: a whale swimming through cloud, lightning bottled, a clock face grown into honeycomb, a key sprouting an eye, spring drawn out of a drawer, rain falling inside a light bulb. Every composition is centred and symmetrical, in a thin gold rim with a rivet above and below. Rules: an emblem tells exactly one story, and if it can't tell it clearly, it picks a different idea.

toys.zh: 二十件中国旧时玩具：空竹、陀螺、毽子、沙燕风筝、走马灯、九连环、七巧板、鲁班锁、拨浪鼓、不倒翁、纸翻花、竹蜻蜓、风车、布老虎、兔儿爷、泥咕咕、糖人、华容道、弹弓、鬃人。竹木铜纸各有各的手艺脾气，磨旧了、发黄了、开裂了，都留着。规矩：都是给人玩的，不许拿去拆——除了鲁班锁，它本来就是给你拆的。
toys.en: Twenty old Chinese toys: a diabolo, a spinning top, a jianzi, a swallow kite, a revolving lantern, nine linked rings, a tangram, a Luban lock, a pellet drum, a tumbler doll, a paper flip flower, a bamboo dragonfly, a pinwheel, a cloth tiger, a clay rabbit lord, a nigugu bird, a sugar figurine, a Klotski board, a bamboo slingshot and a bristle horse. Bamboo, wood, bronze and paper each carry their own temperament, worn pale, yellowed and split but all kept. Rules: these are for playing with, not for taking apart — except the Luban lock, which exists to be taken apart.

playkids.zh: 六个玩得起劲的孩子：抖空竹、踢毽子、放风筝、捧走马灯、摇拨浪鼓、抽陀螺。红袄绿裤、黄马甲蓝裤子，脚下踩着自己的影子就笑。规矩：只管玩，别数摔了几次，也别问为什么风筝线断了——那是风的事。
playkids.en: Six kids thoroughly absorbed in play: working a diabolo, kicking a jianzi, flying a kite, carrying a revolving lantern, shaking a pellet drum, whipping a spinning top. Red jackets and green trousers, yellow vests and blue pants, laughing with a shadow under their feet. Rules: just play, don't count the falls, and don't ask why the kite string snapped — that's the wind's business.

vehicles.zh: 从复古火箭到碟形光束船，动力系统一律不可考。但只要背景是星空，速度感就成立。
vehicles.en: From retro rockets to disc-shaped beam ships, the propulsion is unverifiable — but against a starfield, a sense of speed simply holds.

aliens.zh: 果克星球及周边星域的原住民集中区。大头、多眼、甲壳与凝胶是本地四大主流长相，审美统一得令人怀疑他们有同一个居委会。
aliens.en: The natives of Guck and neighbouring systems. Big heads, many eyes, carapace and gel are the four local looks — so unified you suspect a single neighbourhood committee.

flora.zh: 不进行光合作用，主要进行造型竞争。螺旋星藤在本分类常年人气第一，因为它连缠绕都缠得很有构图意识。
flora.en: No photosynthesis here — only a competition in silhouette. The spiral star-vine tops the category year-round because even its coiling shows compositional awareness.

stoneage.zh: 燧石、骨器与兽皮，人类最早的一批开源硬件。本站收藏它们，是为了提醒后人：好设计不需要充电口。
stoneage.en: Flint, bone and hide — humanity's first open-source hardware. Collected here to remind later generations that good design needs no charging port.

potions.zh: 品红、幽蓝、荧光绿，颜色越不可能越有效。本分类所有瓶子的保质期都是永远，功效请自行想象。
potions.en: Magenta, abyssal blue, fluorescent green — the more improbable the colour, the more potent. Every bottle here keeps forever; effects are left to your imagination.

books.zh: 血皮、烫金、会自己翻页。本站的法典一律只借不卖，而且不保证读完。
books.en: Blood-red leather, gilt edges, pages that turn themselves. The grimoires here are lend-only, never sold — and completion is not guaranteed.

implements.zh: 魔杖、护符与来路不明的发光棍子。共同点是：拿在谁手里都像主角，这就是法器界的公平。
implements.en: Wands, talismans and glowing sticks of unclear origin. Their shared trait: whoever holds one looks like the protagonist — the great fairness of implements.

castles.zh: 浮空岛堡与山坡石堡，建筑规范全部作废，唯一起重机是想象力。住在这里的公主一般自己打怪。
castles.en: Floating-island forts and hillside stone keeps, with every building code void — the only crane is imagination. Princesses here typically slay their own monsters.

furniture.zh: 旧橡木长桌领衔。每件家具都自带一段没人记得的往事，以及恰到好处的裂纹——那是岁月的正版防伪标。
furniture.en: Led by the old oak table, each piece carries a past no one recalls and a perfectly placed crack — time's authentic anti-counterfeit mark.

techdev.zh: 全息投影仪与来路不明的读数装置。本站科技树的特征是：线头比功能多，但看着就是很厉害。
techdev.en: Holo-projectors and dials of unclear purpose. The site's tech tree is defined by more cables than functions — yet it always looks impressive.

xenohorror.zh: 折光伏击者等掠食者专区。它们捕猎不为果腹，主要为构图——毕竟出现在图鉴里比出现在晚餐里更永恒。
xenohorror.en: A zone for ambush predators. They hunt not for food but for composition — appearing in a gallery, after all, outlasts appearing in a dinner.

badges.zh: 低音核、蒸汽卡车与步枪，三枚一组的小型荣誉体系。别在胸前不涨工资，但能明确传达「此人有所热爱」。
badges.en: Bass cores, steam trucks and rifles — a compact honours system in sets of three. They raise no salary, but they clearly state that this person loves something.

planets.zh: 碎环星领衔的星球徽章库，每颗星都经过认真的虚构登记。它们不公转，只负责在深蓝背景上好看。
planets.en: A registry of planet sigils led by the shattered-ring world, each formally fictional. They orbit nothing; their duty is to look good on deep blue.

motion.zh: 挖矿、钓鱼、射击三个循环小动画，Remotion 一帧帧渲染出来的。小人们活得很充实，而且永远不会累。
motion.en: Three looping animations — mining, fishing, shooting — rendered frame by frame in Remotion. The little figures live full lives and never tire.

instruments.zh: 螺壳号与 U 形琴，吹奏效果一律待考。本站乐器的音准由演奏者的信心决定。
instruments.en: Shell horns and U-shaped zithers, all of unverified effect. Here an instrument's pitch is decided by the player's confidence.

physics.zh: 弩炮与天平，靠杠杆和扭力吃饭的正经机械。在魔法横行的站里，它们代表最后的工程学尊严。
physics.en: Ballistae and balances — honest machines fed by leverage and torsion. On a site full of magic, they stand for engineering's last dignity.

scarecrows.zh: 南瓜头、四臂、会自己挪位置。农田雇它们防鸟，现在它们主要防的是访客的胆量。
scarecrows.en: Pumpkin heads, four arms and a habit of relocating overnight. Farms hired them against birds; nowadays they guard against visitors' courage.

fangs.zh: 环牙巨口挂帅。本分类的牙齿数量经过审计，每一颗都有排班表。
fangs.en: Led by the ringed maw, the tooth count here has been audited — every fang keeps a roster.

astones.zh: 熔裂石与结晶岩，外星地质学的样品柜。它们不说话，但每一道纹理都是亿万年的会议纪要。
astones.en: Fused stones and crystal rocks — the sample cabinet of alien geology. They say nothing, yet every vein is minutes from a billion-year meeting.

currency.zh: 星纹圆币等外星通货。本站一律不设汇率，因为拿回地球也花不出去。
currency.en: Alien currency such as star-patterned discs. No exchange rate is published — none of it spends back on Earth.

symbols.zh: 青铜符碑上的未知文字，语法完整但无人能读。破译工作本站已外包给未来。
symbols.en: Unknown scripts on bronze steles — complete grammar, no readers. Deciphering has been outsourced to the future.

ships.zh: 碟形光束船领衔。本分类飞船的泊位一律设在图鉴背景的星空里，违章不贴条。
ships.en: Led by the disc-shaped beam ship, all craft here berth in the gallery's starfield — parking violations are not ticketed.

spaceweapons.zh: 青光能量步枪等。设计原则是把杀伤力做成肉眼可见的样子，毕竟真空里没人听得见巨响。
spaceweapons.en: Cyan energy rifles and the like, designed so lethality is visible — in a vacuum nobody hears the bang anyway.

flyboots.zh: 喷气皮靴，个人航空的最短路径。本分类不提供降落伞退款服务。
flyboots.en: Jet boots — the shortest path to personal aviation. No parachute refunds in this category.

shields.zh: 铆钉木圆盾等。防御面积与审美面积成正比，这是本分类唯一的物理学。
shields.en: Riveted wooden rounds and the like. Here coverage scales with beauty — the category's only physics.

energyblocks.zh: 星核晶块等发光方块。握在手里会让人想喊口号，本站对此现象不做解释。
energyblocks.en: Glowing cubes such as the star core. Held in hand they inspire shouting; this site offers no explanation.

morphmonsters.zh: 凝胶变形兽，形态自由。本分类的物种边界由心情决定。
morphmonsters.en: Gel morph-beasts of free form. Species boundaries here are decided by mood.

telescopes.zh: U 形怀表镜等。看远处很清楚，看近处更不清楚——本分类的统一遗憾。
telescopes.en: U-shaped pocket scopes and the like: excellent at distance, worse up close — the category's shared regret.

crafts.zh: 手绣花布胸针领衔的暖土色手作系。本站刻意避开霓虹科技风之后，针脚终于有了落脚处。
crafts.en: A warm-earth handmade line led by embroidered brooches. After deliberately avoiding neon tech, the stitches finally found a home.

riders.zh: 青铜面具武士骑六足蜈蚣。坐骑越冷门，武士的气场越稳，这是本分类的守恒律。
riders.en: Bronze-masked warriors astride six-legged centipedes. The more obscure the mount, the steadier the aura — a conservation law here.

bgun.zh: 兽角喇叭铳等怪奇手作风火器。材质一律奇诡，扳机手感由想象力提供。
bgun.en: Horn-trumpet guns and other hand-made oddities, of curious make — trigger feel supplied by imagination.

modern.zh: 外卖骑手领衔的现代日常职业装束小人。他们不上朝，只上工，装束扁平但心事矢量。
modern.en: Modern-daily figures led by the delivery rider. They attend no court, only work — flat of costume, vector of worry.

oldfolk.zh: 护目镜怪老头等。本分类老人的年龄介于「很久」与「非常久」之间，道具比岁数更说明问题。
oldfolk.en: Goggle-wearing eccentrics and the like, aged between quite old and very old — their props explain more than their years.

imp.zh: 火苗小鬼等。破坏力与身高成正比，闯祸后的道歉速度也是。
imp.en: Flame imps and the like, whose destructive power scales with height — as does the speed of their apologies.

flybeast.zh: 鬃毛翼狮兽等。起飞不需要跑道，降落看心情。
flybeast.en: Maned winged lions and the like: takeoff needs no runway; landing depends on mood.

oddplants.zh: 笑脸蛛腿花领衔。本分类的授粉工作由错觉完成。
oddplants.en: Led by the smiling spider-leg flower, pollination here is performed by illusion.

jewels.zh: 太阳脸金项坠等。本分类的金属光泽经过审计，耀眼光度全部真实。
jewels.en: Sun-faced gold pendants and the like, with audited metal lustre — the shine is entirely real.

fairykid.zh: 羽衣仙童等胖娃娃中式仙童。不腾云，只迈着小短腿赶路，仙气全靠表情撑住。
fairykid.en: Feather-robed chubby immortal children who never ride clouds — only hurry on short legs, bearing their air entirely on expression.

foodjar.zh: 泡星光罐等。内容物不可名状，保存期限写的是「直到世界尽头」。
foodjar.en: Star-pickle jars and the like, of unnameable contents, stamped best before the end of the world.

hairyboot.zh: 卷毛短靴领衔。保暖性能存疑，卖萌性能超标。
hairyboot.en: Led by curly-haired ankle boots: warmth unverified, cuteness over quota.

oddbug.zh: 多眼毛虫等。本分类的复眼数量经不起细数，建议远观。
oddbug.en: Many-eyed caterpillars and the like — the compound eyes defy counting, so viewing from afar is advised.

constellation.zh: 茶壶座等虚构星点连线。天文学界尚未承认，酒吧讲故事的场合已经常用。
constellation.en: Fictional constellations such as the Teapot — unacknowledged by astronomy, already common at bars.

nonsense.zh: 顶鱼礼帽先生领衔。逻辑已让位，体面仍在维持，这就是本分类的表演张力。
nonsense.en: Led by the fish-hatted gentleman: logic has abdicated yet dignity holds — that is the category's tension.

retrofolk.zh: 迪斯科舞王等复古故事书风冷脸人物。他们从旧画报里走出来，对新时代保持礼貌的冷淡。
retrofolk.en: Disco kings and other cold-faced storybook retros, stepped out of old magazines, politely cool toward the new age.

fusionfolk.zh: 滑板侠客等。时间线在他们身上达成了幽默的和解。
fusionfolk.en: Skateboarding knights-errant and the like — timelines reach a humorous settlement on them.

blades.zh: 弯钩齿轮镰等手动近战冷兵器。形状越诡异，越说明设计者没打算让它量产。
blades.en: Hook-gear scythes and other melee oddities — the stranger the shape, the clearer it was never meant for mass production.

giantfolk.zh: 弯角杂货巨人等。体型是优势也是货架：他们兼职给小镇当移动商店。
giantfolk.en: Twist-horned grocery giants and the like, whose size is both advantage and shelf — they double as the town's mobile shop.

skulls.zh: 齿轮骷髅等。骨头与机械的合资企业，死后比生前更有结构感。
skulls.en: Gearwork skulls and the like — bone-and-machine joint ventures, more structured in death than in life.

oddweapons.zh: 扳手权杖等。工具与武器的身份争议在本分类长期悬置。
oddweapons.en: Wrench sceptres and the like, where the tool-or-weapon question stays permanently open.

monstertoys.zh: 被小孩玩坏、又被缝补起来的玩具们的再就业现场。橡胶、铁皮、毛线与针线在本分类和平共处，共同原则是：一只眼睛也照样营业。
monstertoys.en: Where toys broken by children come back for a second career. Rubber, tin, yarn and stitching coexist here under one rule: one eye is still open for business.

oddbeasts.zh: 进化论管不到的地区。长颈套铁环的、拿伞骨当壳的、三头叠一摞的，走法各不相同，但都准时出现在图鉴里亮相。
oddbeasts.en: The region evolution forgot. Iron-ringed necks, umbrella-rib shells, three heads stacked in a pile — they all walk differently, yet all appear on schedule.

deepfish.zh: 深海没有构图压力，所以随便长长就行。本分类居民一律表情听天由命，身上自带照明，牙比道理多。
deepfish.en: The deep sea applies no compositional pressure, so anything goes. Its residents look resigned, carry their own lighting, and own more teeth than sense.

oddbirds.zh: 鸟纲之下、常识之上。脖子能吹萨克斯，嘴是汤勺，尾巴是小号，后背能冒蒸汽——本分类证明羽毛只是可选项。
oddbirds.en: Below Aves, above common sense. Necks that play saxophones, beaks are spoons, tails are trumpets, backs steam — proof that feathers are optional.

hardware.zh: 开锁的、撬门的、拧螺丝的，全挤在本分类。按材质分：铁的负责沉，黄铜的负责旧，锈的负责说明年代。用途只有一个——让人以为门还锁着。
hardware.en: Lock-pickers, door-breakers and bolt-turners all crowd this category. By material: iron for weight, brass for age, rust for the date. Their only real job is to make a door look locked.

toyfolk.zh: PVC 软胶公仔专区，全是圆头圆脑的塑料小人与小兽。它们不会玩，只负责被摆在货架上、被人捏一下、然后回到原位。
toyfolk.en: A shelf of soft PVC figures: round-headed plastic children and beasts. They don't play, they just stand on the shelf, get squeezed once, and return to their spot.

fairytale.zh: 19 世纪欧洲故事书的插画活页。水彩加细墨线，暖调克制，配色讲究得像印刷厂校对过。本分类的规矩是：所有故事都停在最要紧的那一页之前。
fairytale.en: Loose leaves from a 19th-century European storybook: delicate ink lines over soft watercolour, warm and restrained, colour-checked as if the printer had proofread it. House rule: every story stops one page before the crucial one.

alienfolk.zh: 外星人终于学会了穿衣服。燕尾服、和服、旗袍、军礼服、帝王袍轮番登场，说明它们缺的不是布料，是场合。本分类只收盛装，不收便服。
alienfolk.en: Aliens have finally learned to dress. Tailcoats, kimonos, qipaos, dress uniforms and imperial robes take turns, proving what they lacked was never cloth but occasion. This category accepts formal wear only.

oddchem.zh: 玻璃器皿里装着讲不通的配方。冷凝管会自己盘成蛇，烧瓶能套三层，最细的那支量筒里泡着一整片夜空。本分类的规矩：能读刻度，不许问刻的是什么。
oddchem.en: Glassware holding recipes that refuse to make sense. Condensers coil into snakes, flasks nest three deep, and the finest cylinder soaks up an entire night sky. House rule: you may read the graduations, not ask what is being measured.

trades.zh: 八位靠手艺吃饭的旧式匠人，一个比一个实在。箍桶的、修表的、缝皮的、弹棉的、磨刀的、扎纸的、染布的、编竹的，全站在同一片纸底上，谁也没比谁体面。规矩只有一条：手上的东西不许假。
trades.en: Eight old craftspeople who live by their hands, each more grounded than the last. A cooper, a clockmaker, a leatherworker, a cotton carder, a knife grinder, a paper artisan, a dyer and a basket weaver, all standing on the same flat ground. One rule: nothing they hold may be fake.

opera.zh: 武生、花旦、花脸、老生、丑角、青衣——六位把脸谱当工牌戴的角儿，全站嗓门最大的一分类。规矩：亮相要稳，水袖要飘，白鼻梁不许擦掉。他们不上台，只在透明背景上比画架势。
opera.en: Wusheng, huadan, jing, laosheng, chou and qingyi — six performers wearing painted faces as their staff badges, the loudest category on the site. Rules: hold the pose, float the sleeves, never wipe the white nose patch. They never take a stage; they only gesture against a transparent background.

seamonsters.zh: 深海是本站唯一没有营业执照的车间。海龙、克拉肯、巨蟹、水母、海象魔、灯笼鱼，全是浪花里长出来的住户，鳞片与触须一律不收税。规矩：上岸可以，别把咸味带进透明背景。它们不攻击船只，只负责让看图的人后退半步。
seamonsters.en: The deep sea is the only workshop here with no business licence. Sea serpents, krakens, crabs, jellies, walrus-fiends and anglerfish, all residents grown from the surf, scales and tentacles tax-free. Rule: you may come ashore, but leave the salt out of the transparent background. They never attack ships — they only make the viewer step back half a pace.

plantfolk.zh: 六株学会穿衣服的植物，把花瓣当衣襟、把叶子当手。礼帽蘑菇、围巾仙人掌、和服荷花、背带裤向日葵、兜帽藤蔓、雨靴郁金香，一个个比园丁还讲究。规矩：花盆可以没有，体面不能没有。它们不结果子，只负责在透明背景上过各自的精致小日子。
plantfolk.en: Six plants that learned to dress, wearing petals as lapels and leaves as hands. A top-hat mushroom, a scarf cactus, a kimono lotus, an overalls sunflower, a hooded ivy and a rainboot tulip, each more fastidious than a gardener. Rule: a pot is optional, dignity is not. They bear no fruit — they only live their neat little lives against a transparent background.

metalfolk.zh: 六个从旧抽屉深处翻出来的金属小人：黄铜矮人、发条少年、青铜骑士、锡皮鼓手、铜锈书吏、镀金园丁，个头不过膝，脾气却各不相同。规矩：擦亮可以，上发条随缘，别把铜绿当锈病治——那是它们的年轮。它们不吵不闹，只在透明背景上过各自的旧日子。
metalfolk.en: Six metal folk dug out of an old drawer: a brass gnome, a clockwork boy, a bronze knight, a tin drummer, a verdigris scribe and a gilded gardener, each knee-high and each in a different mood. Rules: polishing is welcome, winding is optional, and never treat the verdigris as a disease — it is their ring count. They are quiet company, living their old days against a transparent background.
